passages.titleEn: Sudden facial swelling after a restaurant meal
passages.titleZh: 餐厅进食后突发面部肿胀

profile.chiefComplaintEn: Throat tightness and facial swelling, sudden onset
profile.chiefComplaintZh: 咽喉紧缩感与面部肿胀，突然发作
profile.pastMedicalHxEn: Known shellfish allergy; two previous reactions, neither required admission to hospital
profile.pastMedicalHxZh: 已知对贝类过敏；既往两次过敏反应，均未住院
profile.medicationsEn: None. Family states an epinephrine auto-injector was prescribed but it is expired and at home
profile.medicationsZh: 无。家属说医生曾开过 epinephrine 自动注射笔，但已过期且放在家里
profile.firstVitalsEn: HR 124 and regular; RR 28 and shallow; BP 88/54; SpO2 91% on room air
profile.firstVitalsZh: HR 124，规则；RR 28，浅快；BP 88/54；室内空气下 SpO2 91%
profile.physicalFindingsEn: Urticaria over the chest and neck; audible wheeze; swelling of the lips and tongue; anxious but alert
profile.physicalFindingsZh: 胸部与颈部可见 urticaria（荨麻疹）；可闻及 wheeze（哮鸣音）；唇部与舌部肿胀；焦虑但神志清醒
profile.otherInformationEn: Symptoms began within 10 minutes of eating a seafood chowder. The patient walked from his table to the front of the restaurant before staff called 911.
profile.otherInformationZh: 进食海鲜浓汤后 10 分钟内出现症状。在店员拨打 911 之前，患者自己从餐桌走到了餐厅门口。

questions.questionEn: The patient is standing near the restaurant entrance when you reach him. Before any medication is given, what does the BC anaphylaxis guideline direct the EMR to do about his position?
questions.questionZh: 你到达时患者正站在餐厅门口。在给任何药物之前，BC 的 anaphylaxis 指南要求 EMR 如何处理他的体位？

options.en: Sit him upright in a chair and have him lean forward
options.zh: 让他坐在椅子上、身体前倾

options.en: Walk him out to the stretcher at the ambulance door to save time
options.zh: 为了节省时间，让他自己走到停在门口的救护车担架旁

options.en: Lay him supine and do not allow him to walk
options.zh: 让他仰卧（supine），并且不允许他走动

options.en: Place him semi-prone in the recovery position
options.zh: 把他放成半俯卧的复原体位

questions.explanationEn: The BC anaphylaxis guideline states plainly: position supine to improve blood pressure and do not walk the patient. This patient is already hypotensive at 88/54; walking an anaphylactic patient can empty a poorly filled heart and precipitate collapse. Option A is the position used for asthma and COPD, not for a hypotensive anaphylactic patient. Option D is reserved for a patient who cannot protect their own airway; this patient is alert.
questions.explanationZh: BC 的 anaphylaxis 指南写得很直接：仰卧以改善血压，并且不要让患者走动。本例血压已降至 88/54，让 anaphylaxis 患者走动会使本就充盈不足的心脏进一步排空，可能导致虚脱。选项 A 是 asthma / COPD 的体位，不适用于低血压的 anaphylaxis 患者。选项 D 只用于无法自行保护气道的患者，而本例神志清醒。

questions.questionEn: The patient is now supine, high-flow oxygen is running and the wheeze has become louder. What is the correct EMR dose and route of epinephrine for this patient?
questions.questionZh: 患者现已仰卧，高流量氧气已给上，哮鸣音变得更响。对这位患者，EMR 给 epinephrine 的正确剂量与途径是什么？

options.en: 0.3 mg subcutaneous, repeated once after 15 minutes
options.zh: 0.3 mg 皮下注射（subcutaneous），15 分钟后重复一次

options.en: 0.5 mg IM, may be repeated every 5 minutes up to 3 times
options.zh: 0.5 mg IM（肌注），每 5 分钟可重复一次，最多重复 3 次

options.en: 0.01 mg/kg IM to a maximum of 0.3 mg, single dose only
options.zh: 0.01 mg/kg IM，最大 0.3 mg，只给一次

options.en: 0.5 mg IV push, repeated every 5 minutes
options.zh: 0.5 mg IV 推注，每 5 分钟重复一次

questions.explanationEn: The BC monograph gives the adult anaphylaxis dose as 0.5 mg IM every 5 minutes, repeated up to 3 times. Option C is the paediatric weight-based dose (0.01 mg/kg IM to a maximum of 0.5 mg) and would badly under-dose a 28-year-old. Option A uses the wrong route and a dose from an older auto-injector convention. Option D is wrong on route and is outside the EMR scope: EMRs give epinephrine intramuscularly only.
questions.explanationZh: BC 药物专论规定成人 anaphylaxis 的剂量为 0.5 mg IM，每 5 分钟一次，最多重复 3 次。选项 C 是儿科按体重给药（0.01 mg/kg IM，最大 0.5 mg），用在 28 岁成人身上会严重剂量不足。选项 A 途径错误，剂量沿用的是旧式自动注射笔的规格。选项 D 途径错误，而且超出 EMR 授权范围——EMR 只能肌注 epinephrine。
questions.evolutionEn: The patient has been laid supine, high-flow oxygen is running, and the audible wheeze has become louder.
questions.evolutionZh: 患者已被放平仰卧，高流量氧气已开始，可闻及的哮鸣音变得更响。

questions.questionEn: Five minutes after the first dose of epinephrine the wheeze persists, the blood pressure is now 82/50 and SpO2 is 90% on high-flow oxygen. Your partner has brought the stretcher alongside the patient. What is the most appropriate action?
questions.questionZh: 第一剂 epinephrine 后 5 分钟，哮鸣音仍在，血压降至 82/50，高流量氧气下 SpO2 为 90%。搭档已把担架推到患者身旁。此时最恰当的处置是什么？

options.en: Give a second dose of epinephrine 0.5 mg IM and initiate transport
options.zh: 再给第二剂 epinephrine 0.5 mg IM，并开始转运

options.en: Give salbutamol by nebulizer and reassess in five minutes before deciding about transport
options.zh: 先用 nebulizer 给 salbutamol，5 分钟后复评再决定是否转运

options.en: Stay on scene to complete a detailed head-to-toe examination before moving him
options.zh: 留在现场完成详细的头到脚检查后再搬动他

options.en: Give diphenhydramine to limit the histamine response
options.zh: 给 diphenhydramine 以抑制组胺反应

questions.explanationEn: The patient is deteriorating despite the first dose, so the repeat dose of epinephrine is due at 5 minutes and transport must not be delayed. Option B is the classic near-miss: salbutamol does treat the bronchospasm and is within EMR scope, but it is an adjunct that follows epinephrine, and pausing five minutes to reassess before deciding about transport wastes time in a patient who is losing his blood pressure. Option C is the standard exam trap of correct-treatment-wrong-priority: a detailed secondary assessment belongs en route, not on scene, in an unstable patient. Option D is a PCP intervention and is outside the EMR scope.
questions.explanationZh: 第一剂后患者仍在恶化，因此 5 分钟时应给第二剂 epinephrine，并且不能再延误转运。选项 B 是典型的「差一点就对」：salbutamol 确实能缓解支气管痉挛，也在 EMR 范围内，但它是 epinephrine 之后的辅助手段；而且在一个血压正在掉的患者身上停下来观察 5 分钟再决定转不转，是在浪费时间。选项 C 是经典陷阱——处置本身没错但优先级错了：不稳定患者的详细二次评估应在转运途中做，而不是留在现场做。选项 D 属于 PCP 的处置，超出 EMR 范围。
questions.evolutionEn: Five minutes have passed since the first epinephrine dose. The wheeze persists, BP has fallen from 88/54 to 82/50, and SpO2 is 90% despite high-flow oxygen. The stretcher is now beside the patient.
questions.evolutionZh: 距第一剂 epinephrine 已过 5 分钟。哮鸣音仍在，血压由 88/54 降至 82/50，高流量氧气下 SpO2 为 90%。担架已推到患者身旁。

questions.questionEn: Immediately after the injection your partner hands you the used syringe and needle. The patient is being moved onto the stretcher and the restaurant floor is crowded with customers and staff. What should you do with the sharp?
questions.questionZh: 注射结束后，搭档立刻把用过的注射器和针头递给你。此时患者正被搬上担架，餐厅地面上挤满了顾客和店员。你应该如何处理这个利器？

options.en: Recap the needle and put it in your uniform pocket until you get back to the ambulance
options.zh: 把针帽套回去，放进制服口袋，等回到救护车再处理

options.en: Hand it to a member of the restaurant staff to dispose of
options.zh: 交给餐厅店员去处理

options.en: Wrap it in gauze and put it in the drug kit until the call is finished
options.zh: 用纱布包好放进药箱，等这趟出勤结束再说

options.en: Place it directly into a puncture-resistant sharps container
options.zh: 直接放入防穿刺的 sharps container（利器盒）

questions.explanationEn: Sharps are disposed of immediately into a puncture-resistant container. Every other option leaves an uncontrolled needle in a crowded room: recapping is itself a common cause of needlestick injury, a pocketed or gauze-wrapped needle will be found by the next hand into that pocket or kit, and handing a contaminated sharp to a member of the public transfers your occupational risk to someone with no training and no protection. Occupational safety is examinable in its own right alongside clinical care.
questions.explanationZh: 利器必须立即丢入防穿刺容器。其他每一个选项都会让一根失控的针头留在拥挤的房间里：重新套针帽本身就是针刺伤的常见原因；塞口袋或用纱布包起来放药箱，下一个把手伸进去的人就会中招；把污染利器交给普通市民，等于把你的职业暴露风险转嫁给一个没有受过训练、也没有防护的人。职业安全和临床处置一样，是独立的考点。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.9 (Rescue Scene Evaluation - hazards); CPCF area E
questions.evolutionEn: Epinephrine has been given and the patient is being moved onto the stretcher; the restaurant floor remains crowded.
questions.evolutionZh: epinephrine 已注射完毕，患者正被搬上担架；餐厅内仍然人多拥挤。

profile.chiefComplaintZh: 呼吸困难，6 小时内逐渐加重
profile.pastMedicalHxEn: Asthma diagnosed at age 2; two emergency department visits for asthma this year
profile.pastMedicalHxZh: 2 岁时确诊 asthma（哮喘）；今年已因哮喘两次去急诊
profile.medicationsEn: Salbutamol MDI at home; mother gave 2 puffs one hour ago with little effect
profile.medicationsZh: 家中有 salbutamol MDI（定量吸入器）；母亲 1 小时前给她吸了 2 喷，效果不明显
profile.firstVitalsEn: HR 158; RR 44; SpO2 89% on room air; Temp 37.4 C; weight approximately 17 kg
profile.firstVitalsZh: HR 158；RR 44；室内空气下 SpO2 89%；体温 37.4 C；体重约 17 kg
profile.physicalFindingsEn: Sitting upright and tripoding on her mother's lap; intercostal and subcostal indrawing; expiratory wheeze in all fields; speaking in single words only
profile.physicalFindingsZh: 坐在母亲腿上，身体前倾呈三脚架姿势；肋间与肋下凹陷；双肺满布呼气相哮鸣音；只能一个词一个词地说话
profile.otherInformationEn: The family recently brought a cat into the home. The child is frightened and cries whenever a stranger comes close.
profile.otherInformationZh: 家里最近养了一只猫。孩子很害怕，陌生人一靠近就哭。

questions.questionEn: Which one of the following best describes the correct approach to assessing this child?
questions.questionZh: 以下哪一项最能描述评估这名儿童的正确做法？

options.en: Move her onto the stretcher and lay her supine so a full set of vital signs can be taken
options.zh: 把她抱上担架并放平仰卧，以便测量完整的生命体征

options.en: Separate her from her mother so that she can concentrate on your questions
options.zh: 把她和母亲分开，好让她专心回答你的问题

options.en: Delay all assessment until salbutamol has been given
options.zh: 在给 salbutamol 之前，暂缓一切评估

options.en: Leave her on her mother's lap in the position she has chosen and begin the assessment at her feet
options.zh: 让她保持自己选择的姿势坐在母亲腿上，从脚开始做评估

questions.explanationEn: Two paediatric principles combine here. First, a child in respiratory distress has chosen the tripod position for a reason, and laying her flat or taking her from her mother will increase her work of breathing and her distress. Second, assessment in this age group is conducted toe-to-head to gain the child's confidence before you reach the frightening parts. Option C is an absolute that would have you withhold even the primary survey, which always comes before any protocol.
questions.explanationZh: 这里叠加了两条儿科原则。第一，呼吸窘迫的孩子摆出三脚架姿势是有原因的，把她放平或从母亲怀里抱走，只会加重呼吸做功和恐惧。第二，这个年龄段的评估从脚往头做（toe-to-head），先建立信任，再检查会吓到她的部位。选项 C 是绝对化措辞，等于连 primary survey 都不做了——而初步检查永远在任何 protocol 之前。

questions.questionEn: You have left the child on her mother's lap and oxygen is being held near her face; SpO2 has risen to 92%. According to the BC drug monograph, what is the correct salbutamol dose for this 17 kg child by metered dose inhaler?
questions.questionZh: 你让孩子继续坐在母亲腿上，并把氧气面罩举在她面部附近，SpO2 升至 92%。根据 BC 药物专论，这名 17 kg 儿童用 MDI 给 salbutamol 的正确剂量是多少？

options.en: 4 x 100 mcg, repeated as required
options.zh: 4 x 100 mcg，按需重复

options.en: 5 x 100 mcg per course, may be repeated up to 3 times
options.zh: 每疗程 5 x 100 mcg，最多可重复 3 次

options.en: 10 x 100 mcg per course, may be repeated up to 3 times
options.zh: 每疗程 10 x 100 mcg，最多可重复 3 次

options.en: MDI is not indicated at this weight; she requires 2.5 mg by nebulizer
options.zh: 这个体重不适用 MDI；必须用 nebulizer 给 2.5 mg

questions.explanationEn: Paediatric MDI dosing is banded by weight: under 10 kg MDI is not indicated, 10-20 kg gets 5 x 100 mcg per course, and over 20 kg gets 10 x 100 mcg per course; both bands may be repeated up to 3 times. At 17 kg she falls in the 10-20 kg band. Option A is the adult dose, option C is the over-20 kg dose, and the 2.5 mg nebulizer dose in option D is the dose for a child under one year of age. A spacer should be used with the MDI.
questions.explanationZh: 儿科 MDI 剂量按体重分档：<10 kg 不适用 MDI；10-20 kg 每疗程 5 x 100 mcg；>20 kg 每疗程 10 x 100 mcg；两档均最多可重复 3 次。17 kg 落在 10-20 kg 这一档。选项 A 是成人剂量，选项 C 是 >20 kg 的剂量，选项 D 中 2.5 mg 的雾化剂量是 1 岁以下婴儿的剂量。用 MDI 时应配合 spacer（储雾罐）。
questions.evolutionEn: The child has been left in her position of comfort on her mother's lap and oxygen is being held near her face; SpO2 has come up from 89% to 92%.
questions.evolutionZh: 孩子被保留在母亲腿上的舒适体位，氧气举在她面部附近；SpO2 已从 89% 升至 92%。

questions.questionEn: After two courses of salbutamol the wheeze has become much quieter, the child has stopped crying, her SpO2 is 88% on high-flow oxygen and her head bobs with each breath. What does this change most likely mean, and what should you do?
questions.questionZh: 给了两个疗程的 salbutamol 后，哮鸣音明显变轻，孩子不哭了，高流量氧气下 SpO2 降到 88%，每次呼吸时头部随之点动。这一变化最可能意味着什么？你应该怎么做？

options.en: She is improving; continue salbutamol and complete a detailed secondary assessment on scene
options.zh: 她在好转；继续给 salbutamol，并在现场完成详细的二次评估

options.en: She has an upper airway foreign body; begin back blows and chest thrusts
options.zh: 她有上气道异物；开始拍背和胸部冲击

options.en: She is tiring with falling air entry; assist ventilations with a bag-valve mask and transport immediately
options.zh: 她已疲劳、进气量下降；用 BVM 辅助通气并立即转运

options.en: She now meets the criteria for CPAP; apply it before moving her to the ambulance
options.zh: 她现在符合 CPAP 的适应证；上救护车前先给她上 CPAP

questions.explanationEn: A quiet chest in an asthmatic child is not a good sign — it means too little air is moving to generate a wheeze. Combined with a falling SpO2 despite high-flow oxygen, a child who has gone quiet and a bobbing head, this is exhaustion and impending respiratory failure. The guideline directs you to assist inadequate or failing respirations, which here means bag-valve-mask ventilation and immediate transport. Option A misreads the silence as improvement and adds the on-scene-delay trap. Option B does not fit a six-hour history with a known asthma diagnosis. Option D fails twice: CPAP is contraindicated in patients 12 years and under, and it is a PCP intervention that is outside the EMR scope.
questions.explanationZh: 哮喘患儿肺部变安静不是好事——它意味着进出的气流已经少到吹不出哮鸣音。再加上高流量氧气下 SpO2 仍在下降、孩子不哭了、出现点头样呼吸，这是体力耗竭、即将发生呼吸衰竭。指南要求对不足或衰竭的呼吸进行辅助，在这里就是 BVM 通气并立即转运。选项 A 把「安静」误读成好转，还叠加了现场滞留的陷阱。选项 B 与已确诊哮喘、症状持续 6 小时的病史不符。选项 D 错了两层：CPAP 对 12 岁及以下是禁忌，而且属于 PCP 的处置，超出 EMR 范围。
questions.evolutionEn: Two courses of salbutamol have been given. The wheeze is now much quieter, the child has stopped crying and become quiet, SpO2 has fallen to 88% on high-flow oxygen, and her head bobs with each breath.
questions.evolutionZh: 已给了两个疗程的 salbutamol。哮鸣音明显减弱，孩子从哭闹变得安静，高流量氧气下 SpO2 降至 88%，每次呼吸伴头部点动。

questions.questionEn: The PCP crew has not yet arrived. Which one of the following treatments for this child is outside the EMR scope of practice in British Columbia?
questions.questionZh: PCP 组还没到。在 BC 省，以下哪一项针对这名儿童的处置超出了 EMR 的授权范围？

options.en: Adding ipratropium to a nebulizer
options.zh: 在雾化中加入 ipratropium

options.en: Salbutamol by metered dose inhaler with a spacer
options.zh: 用 MDI 加 spacer 给 salbutamol

options.en: High-flow oxygen by non-rebreather mask
options.zh: 用 non-rebreather 面罩给高流量氧气

options.en: Assisted ventilation with a bag-valve mask
options.zh: 用 BVM 辅助通气

questions.explanationEn: Ipratropium is a PCP-level medication in British Columbia; the EMR bronchodilator is salbutamol, given by MDI with a spacer or by nebulizer. Oxygen and bag-valve-mask ventilation are core EMR skills at every licence level. Knowing where your authorization stops matters as much as knowing the treatment: on the exam, an intervention that is clinically reasonable but above your licence is still the wrong answer. Dexamethasone and CPAP are two other PCP additions in this protocol.
questions.explanationZh: 在 BC 省，ipratropium 属于 PCP 级别药物；EMR 的支气管扩张剂是 salbutamol，可用 MDI 加 spacer 或雾化给药。氧气和 BVM 通气是所有执照等级的核心 EMR 技能。清楚自己的授权边界和掌握处置同样重要：在考试中，一项临床上合理但超出你执照的处置，仍然是错误答案。这个 protocol 里另外两项 PCP 才能做的是 dexamethasone 和 CPAP。
questions.evolutionEn: Bag-valve-mask ventilation has been started and transport is under way; the PCP crew has not yet arrived.
questions.evolutionZh: 已开始 BVM 通气并正在转运途中；PCP 组尚未到达。

passages.titleEn: Confused and sweaty at home before breakfast
passages.titleZh: 早餐前在家中出现意识模糊、大汗

profile.chiefComplaintEn: Found confused and sweaty by her husband, unable to answer questions
profile.chiefComplaintZh: 被丈夫发现意识模糊、大汗，无法回答问题
profile.pastMedicalHxEn: Type 2 diabetes for 18 years; hypertension; mild osteoarthritis
profile.pastMedicalHxZh: 2 型糖尿病 18 年；高血压；轻度骨关节炎
profile.medicationsEn: Long-acting insulin each evening; metformin; ramipril
profile.firstVitalsEn: HR 108; RR 20; BP 142/86; SpO2 96% on room air; BGL 2.4 mmol/L; Temp 36.4 C
profile.firstVitalsZh: HR 108；RR 20；BP 142/86；室内空气下 SpO2 96%；BGL 2.4 mmol/L；体温 36.4 C
profile.physicalFindingsEn: Pale, cool, diaphoretic skin; responds to voice only, with mumbling (AVPU = V); no facial droop; equal grip strength; no signs of injury
profile.physicalFindingsZh: 皮肤苍白、湿冷、大汗；仅对呼唤有含糊应答（AVPU = V）；无口角歪斜；双手握力对称；无外伤征象
profile.otherInformationEn: Her husband says she took her usual insulin last night but skipped both breakfast and lunch because she "wasn't hungry". She was last seen behaving normally 90 minutes ago.
profile.otherInformationZh: 丈夫说她昨晚照常打了 insulin，但今天早餐和午餐都没吃，因为她说「不饿」。最后一次见她表现正常是在 90 分钟前。

questions.questionEn: She responds to voice only, with mumbling, and cannot follow commands. Based on the BC diabetic emergencies guideline, which one of the following is appropriate for the EMR?
questions.questionZh: 她只对呼唤有含糊应答，无法执行指令。根据 BC 的 diabetic emergencies 指南，以下哪一项适合 EMR 执行？

options.en: Place oral glucose gel between the cheek and gum
options.zh: 把 oral glucose gel（葡萄糖凝胶）抹在颊黏膜与牙龈之间

options.en: Withhold all glucose until a PCP crew arrives
options.zh: 在 PCP 组到达前不给任何葡萄糖

options.en: Administer glucagon 1 mg IM
options.zh: 肌注 glucagon 1 mg

options.en: Administer D10W 10-25 g intravenously
options.zh: 静脉给 D10W 10-25 g

questions.explanationEn: The guideline draws the line at mentation: oral glucose gel is applied to the oral mucosa only for patients with sufficient mentation to maintain their own airway. A patient who is at V on AVPU and cannot follow commands does not meet that bar, and for insufficient mentation or an unprotected airway the EMR gives glucagon (0.5-1 mg IM). Option A is the intuitive but unsafe choice and risks aspiration. Option D is a PCP intervention. Option B delays treatment of a BGL of 2.4 mmol/L that the EMR is fully authorized to correct.
questions.explanationZh: 指南以「神志是否足以保护气道」划线：口服葡萄糖凝胶只用于神志足以自行维持气道的患者。AVPU 为 V、无法执行指令的患者达不到这一标准；对神志不足或气道无保护的患者，EMR 应给 glucagon（0.5-1 mg IM）。选项 A 是直觉上想做、但不安全的选择，有误吸风险。选项 D 属于 PCP 的处置。选项 B 会延误对 2.4 mmol/L 低血糖的处理，而这恰恰是 EMR 完全有授权处理的。

questions.questionEn: Glucagon 1 mg has been given IM. She is still at V on AVPU, and her husband now mentions that she vomited once before you arrived. What is the most appropriate way to manage her airway while you wait for a response?
questions.questionZh: 已肌注 glucagon 1 mg。她仍处于 AVPU 的 V 级，丈夫此时补充说，你们到之前她曾吐过一次。在等待药效期间，管理她气道最恰当的方式是什么？

options.en: Place her in the lateral (3/4 prone) position with suction immediately at hand
options.zh: 让她侧卧（3/4 俯卧位），并把吸引装置放在随手可及处

options.en: Insert an oropharyngeal airway and begin bag-valve-mask ventilation
options.zh: 插入 OPA 并开始 BVM 通气

options.en: Sit her fully upright on the edge of the bed and have suction ready
options.zh: 让她完全坐直在床沿，并准备好吸引

options.en: Leave her supine and flat with a nasopharyngeal airway in place
options.zh: 让她平躺仰卧，插入 NPA

questions.explanationEn: The diabetic emergencies guideline specifically directs positioning in the lateral or 3/4 prone position if needed, and the AVPU table says a patient responding only to voice may be placed semi-prone if injuries permit. She has vomited once and cannot fully protect her airway, so gravity and ready suction are the priority. Option B over-treats a patient who is breathing at 20 with an SpO2 of 96% and who still has a gag reflex — an OPA in that patient will provoke vomiting. Option D leaves her supine, the position most likely to end in aspiration.
questions.explanationZh: diabetic emergencies 指南明确要求「必要时置于侧卧或 3/4 俯卧位」，AVPU 表也说明仅对呼唤有反应的患者，在伤情允许时可置半俯卧位。她已呕吐过一次、无法完全保护气道，因此靠重力引流并随时可吸引是首要考虑。选项 B 属于过度处置——她呼吸 20 次/分、SpO2 96%，且仍有咽反射，此时插 OPA 反而会诱发呕吐。选项 D 让她仰卧平躺，这是最容易发生误吸的体位。
questions.evolutionEn: Glucagon 1 mg IM has been given. She remains at V on AVPU, and the husband has now disclosed that she vomited once before your arrival.
questions.evolutionZh: 已肌注 glucagon 1 mg。她仍为 AVPU 的 V 级，丈夫此时才说出你们到达之前她曾呕吐过一次。

questions.questionEn: Ten minutes later she is alert and oriented, her repeat BGL is 6.8 mmol/L, and she says: "Oh dear, I'm so embarrassed. I've wasted your whole evening over a bit of low sugar. Just go — I'll eat a sandwich and lie down." What is the EMR's most appropriate response?
questions.questionZh: 10 分钟后她神志清醒、定向力正常，复测 BGL 为 6.8 mmol/L。她说：「哎呀，真不好意思。就为了一点低血糖，浪费你们一整晚。你们走吧——我吃个三明治躺一会儿就好。」EMR 最恰当的回应是什么？

options.en: "No problem at all. Give us a call again if it happens twice more."
options.zh: 「没事的。如果再发作两次，你再打给我们。」

options.en: "You haven't wasted anyone's evening — this is exactly what we're here for. But because your insulin is a long-acting one and you've missed two meals, your sugar can drop again after we leave, so we'd like to take you in to be checked."
options.zh: 「您一点也没有浪费谁的时间——我们就是为这种情况来的。不过您打的是长效 insulin，又漏了两顿饭，我们走了之后血糖还可能再掉下去，所以我们希望送您去医院检查一下。」

options.en: "You should really be more careful about eating when you're on insulin."
options.zh: 「您打 insulin 的时候真该多注意吃饭。」

options.en: "That's your decision. Sign here and we'll be on our way."
options.zh: 「那是您自己的决定。在这里签个字，我们就走了。」

questions.explanationEn: A communication item needs both halves to be right: the tone has to answer the worry the patient actually voiced, and the clinical instruction has to be safe. Option B relieves her embarrassment and then gives her a concrete, honest reason to come in. Option A is warm but tells her to wait for two more episodes, which is dangerous advice. Option C is technically true and lands as a scolding of an elderly patient who is already embarrassed. Option D accepts a refusal without ever telling her what she is refusing, so any consent she gives is not informed.
questions.explanationZh: 沟通题必须两半都对：语气要回应患者真正说出口的顾虑，临床指令必须安全。选项 B 先化解她的尴尬，再给出一个具体、诚实的就医理由。选项 A 语气温和，却让她等到再发作两次，这是危险的建议。选项 C 内容也许没错，但对一位本已难为情的老人来说就是训话。选项 D 在从未告诉她「她拒绝的是什么」的情况下就接受了拒绝，那样得到的同意根本谈不上知情。
questions.evolutionEn: Ten minutes after glucagon, she is alert and oriented and the repeat BGL is 6.8 mmol/L.
questions.evolutionZh: 给 glucagon 后 10 分钟，她神志清醒、定向力正常，复测 BGL 为 6.8 mmol/L。

questions.questionEn: Her husband asks why she cannot simply eat and stay home now that she is awake. What is the strongest clinical reason to transport her?
questions.questionZh: 丈夫问：既然人已经醒了，为什么不能就在家吃点东西、留在家里？支持转运她的最有力临床理由是什么？

options.en: Metformin commonly causes rebound hypoglycemia within an hour
options.zh: metformin 常在 1 小时内引起反跳性低血糖

options.en: Ramipril blocks the effect of glucagon and will make the blood sugar fall again
options.zh: ramipril 会阻断 glucagon 的作用，使血糖再次下降

options.en: Every patient who receives glucagon must be transported, without exception
options.zh: 凡是用过 glucagon 的患者都必须转运，没有例外

options.en: Glucagon works by releasing the liver's stored glycogen, which may be limited after two missed meals, while her long-acting insulin is still working
options.zh: glucagon 是靠释放肝脏储存的 glycogen 起效的，而她已漏了两顿饭、糖原储备可能有限，与此同时她的长效 insulin 仍在起作用

questions.explanationEn: The reasoning that matters here is the mismatch in duration. Glucagon mobilizes hepatic glycogen, so it works only as long as those stores last, and stores are depleted in a patient who has not eaten all day; her long-acting insulin, meanwhile, will keep working for hours. She is very likely to relapse at home. Option C is the absolute-wording distractor: rules stated as "without exception" are usually the wrong answer, and it also gives her husband no reason he can actually understand. Options A and B invent pharmacology that neither drug has.
questions.explanationZh: 这里真正关键的推理是「作用时长不匹配」。glucagon 靠动员肝糖原起效，因此只能维持到糖原耗尽为止；而她一整天没吃东西，储备很可能本来就不多。与此同时，她的长效 insulin 还会继续作用好几个小时。她在家再次发作的可能性很高。选项 C 是绝对化措辞的干扰项：以「没有例外」表述的规则通常是错的，而且这句话也没给丈夫一个他真能听懂的理由。选项 A、B 编造了这两种药并不具备的药理作用。
questions.evolutionEn: She is now alert with a BGL of 6.8 mmol/L; her husband is questioning the need for hospital.
questions.evolutionZh: 她现在神志清醒，BGL 为 6.8 mmol/L；丈夫正在质疑是否有必要去医院。

passages.titleEn: Fall down the stairs on a blood thinner
passages.titleZh: 服用抗凝药的老人跌落楼梯

profile.chiefComplaintEn: Fell down four carpeted stairs at home and struck the back of his head; now has a headache and neck pain
profile.chiefComplaintZh: 在家中从四级铺地毯的台阶上跌落，后脑着地；现有头痛与颈部疼痛
profile.pastMedicalHxEn: Atrial fibrillation; hypertension; right hip replacement 6 years ago; cataracts
profile.pastMedicalHxZh: 心房颤动（atrial fibrillation）；高血压；6 年前右髋关节置换；白内障
profile.firstVitalsEn: HR 62 and irregular; RR 18; BP 168/92; SpO2 95% on room air; BGL 6.1 mmol/L; GCS 15
profile.firstVitalsZh: HR 62，不规则；RR 18；BP 168/92；室内空气下 SpO2 95%；BGL 6.1 mmol/L；GCS 15
profile.physicalFindingsEn: 4 cm boggy swelling over the occiput with slow ongoing bleeding; midline cervical tenderness on palpation; no limb weakness; pupils equal and reactive
profile.physicalFindingsZh: 枕部 4 cm 松软肿胀，仍有缓慢渗血；颈椎正中线触痛；四肢无肌力下降；双侧瞳孔等大、对光反应存在
profile.otherInformationEn: The fall was not witnessed. He says he "just missed the last step". His daughter states he has been his normal self all day. He is refusing hospital because his dog is home alone.
profile.otherInformationZh: 无人目击跌倒过程。他说自己「只是踩空了最后一级」。女儿说他一整天状态如常。他拒绝去医院，因为家里的狗没人照看。

questions.questionEn: Which one of the findings in this profile most clearly indicates that this patient requires spinal motion restriction?
questions.questionZh: 在这份患者资料中，哪一项发现最明确地提示这位患者需要进行脊柱运动限制（spinal motion restriction）？

options.en: Midline cervical spine tenderness on palpation
options.zh: 颈椎正中线触痛

options.en: His age of 84 years on its own
options.zh: 单凭他 84 岁的年龄

options.en: The bleeding wound on the back of his head
options.zh: 后脑那处仍在出血的伤口

options.en: His irregular heart rate
options.zh: 他不规则的心率

questions.explanationEn: Spinal management in BC follows the NEXUS criteria and the Canadian C-Spine rule, and midline cervical tenderness is a direct positive finding under both. Age is a modifier within the Canadian C-Spine rule rather than a finding that decides the question by itself, so option B overstates it. Option C is a distractor built on a true fact — an obvious injury above the level of the clavicles is a listed indication for cervical stabilization in the primary survey — but the definite, protocol-level finding here is the midline tenderness he is reporting. Option D reflects his known atrial fibrillation and has nothing to do with his spine.
questions.explanationZh: BC 的脊柱处理遵循 NEXUS 标准与 Canadian C-Spine 规则，颈椎正中线触痛在两套标准里都是直接的阳性发现。年龄在 Canadian C-Spine 规则中是一个修正因素，而不是单独就能定论的发现，所以选项 B 说过头了。选项 C 是建立在一个真事实上的干扰项——初步检查中，锁骨平面以上的明显外伤确实是颈部固定的指征之一——但本例中最确凿、直接对应标准的，是他自己报告的正中线触痛。选项 D 反映的是他已知的房颤，与脊柱无关。

questions.questionEn: A hard collar is on and the patient has been log-rolled onto a spinal device. The occipital wound is still oozing and has soaked through the first dressing. What is the most appropriate next step to control this bleeding?
questions.questionZh: 硬颈托已固定，患者已被轴向翻身移至脊柱固定装置上。枕部伤口仍在渗血，已浸透第一层敷料。控制出血的下一步，最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Pack the wound with hemostatic gauze
options.zh: 用止血纱布填塞（pack）伤口

options.en: Apply firm direct pressure with a second dressing placed on top of the first
options.zh: 在第一层敷料上再加一层，持续加压

options.en: Apply a tourniquet proximal to the wound
options.zh: 在伤口近端上止血带

options.en: Remove the soaked dressing, clean the wound and apply a fresh pressure dressing
options.zh: 撕掉已浸透的敷料，清创后换一块新的加压敷料

questions.explanationEn: The BC order of preference for hemorrhage control starts with direct pressure and a pressure dressing, and this scalp bleed has not yet had a proper trial of that. Wound packing is reserved for bleeding that direct pressure cannot control in an area not amenable to a tourniquet, and the guideline explicitly says not to pack wounds on the neck, chest or abdomen — an occipital wound sits right at that boundary and needs pressure, not packing. A tourniquet cannot be applied to the head at all. Option D is the one that actively causes harm: stripping off a soaked dressing pulls away the clot that has already formed, which matters far more in a patient on apixaban.
questions.explanationZh: BC 的止血手段有优先顺序，第一位是直接压迫和加压包扎，而这处头皮出血还没有经过一次像样的加压尝试。伤口填塞只用于直接压迫无法控制、且部位不适合上止血带的出血；指南还明确写明颈部、胸部、腹部的伤口不得填塞——枕部正处在这条边界上，应该加压而不是填塞。头部根本无法使用止血带。选项 D 是会主动造成伤害的那个：撕掉浸透的敷料会把已经形成的血凝块一起扯掉，对一个正在服用 apixaban 的患者来说后果更严重。
questions.evolutionEn: A hard collar has been applied and the patient has been log-rolled onto a spinal device. The occipital wound continues to ooze and has soaked through the first dressing.
questions.evolutionZh: 已上硬颈托，患者被轴向翻身固定到脊柱装置上。枕部伤口持续渗血，已浸透第一层敷料。

questions.questionEn: En route the patient is still GCS 15, but he tells you his headache is getting worse and that he now feels "a bit sick to my stomach". What is the most significant concern raised by this change?
questions.questionZh: 转运途中患者 GCS 仍为 15，但他说头痛在加重，而且现在「有点想吐」。这一变化最值得担心的是什么？

options.en: He is having a vasovagal reaction to the hard collar
options.zh: 他对硬颈托产生了迷走神经反应

options.en: His blood pressure medication is wearing off
options.zh: 他的降压药药效正在消退

options.en: He is becoming hypoglycemic after missing his evening meal
options.zh: 他晚饭没吃，正在出现低血糖

options.en: He is developing an intracranial bleed, which apixaban makes both more likely and more severe
options.zh: 他正在发生颅内出血，而 apixaban 会让这种出血更容易发生、也更严重

questions.explanationEn: A worsening headache with new nausea after a head strike is the classic early picture of a rising intracranial bleed, and the anticoagulant in his medication list is the single most important fact in this profile: on apixaban a bleed that would have been minor can become life-threatening, and it can declare itself hours after a fall that looked trivial. A normal GCS does not exclude it. Option C is excluded by the profile itself — his BGL is documented at 6.1 mmol/L, and the exam convention is that a value given as normal stays normal unless the passage says otherwise. Options A and B do not explain a progressive headache.
questions.explanationZh: 头部受撞后头痛加重并新出现恶心，是颅内出血逐渐增大的典型早期表现；而用药清单里的抗凝药是整份资料中最重要的一条：服用 apixaban 时，原本轻微的出血可能变成致命出血，而且可能在一次看起来微不足道的跌倒之后数小时才显现。GCS 正常并不能排除它。选项 C 已被资料本身排除——BGL 明确记录为 6.1 mmol/L；考试惯例是：资料里给出的正常值，除非后文另有说明，就按正常处理。选项 A、B 都无法解释进行性加重的头痛。
questions.evolutionEn: The patient is now packaged and en route. GCS remains 15, but the headache is worsening and he reports new nausea.
questions.evolutionZh: 患者已固定完毕并在转运途中。GCS 仍为 15，但头痛在加重，并新出现恶心。

questions.questionEn: Before he was packaged, the patient said: "I'm not going anywhere — Buster's been shut in since this morning and there's nobody to feed him." What was the EMR's most appropriate response?
questions.questionZh: 在固定搬运之前，患者说：「我哪儿也不去——Buster 从今天早上就被关在家里，没人喂它。」EMR 最恰当的回应是什么？

options.en: "You have the right to refuse. Sign this form and we'll leave you our number."
options.zh: 「您有权拒绝。在这张表上签个字，我们把电话留给您。」

options.en: "If you don't come with us tonight you could die in your sleep."
options.zh: 「今晚您要是不跟我们走，可能睡着睡着就没命了。」

options.en: "I understand Buster matters — let's sort that out. Is there a neighbour or family member who could take him tonight? You're on a blood thinner and you hit your head, and that kind of bleed can start hours later, so you do need to be seen."
options.zh: 「我明白 Buster 对您很重要——我们先把它安排好。有没有邻居或家人今晚能帮忙照看？您在吃抗凝药，又撞到了头，这类出血可能几个小时之后才开始，所以您确实需要去医院看一下。」

options.en: "Your daughter can decide for you — I'll ask her to sign the consent."
options.zh: 「让您女儿替您做决定吧——我去请她签同意书。」

questions.explanationEn: The barrier he named is the dog, so the answer has to solve the dog and then give him a safe, honest reason to come in. Option C does both. Option A treats his refusal as final without ever explaining what he is risking, so the refusal is not informed. Option B is coercion by fear, which damages trust and often hardens the refusal. Option D bypasses a patient who is GCS 15, alert and oriented, and therefore capable of making his own decision — a competent adult's family does not consent on his behalf.
questions.explanationZh: 他自己说出口的障碍是那条狗，所以正确答案必须先解决狗的问题，再给他一个安全而诚实的就医理由。选项 C 两件事都做到了。选项 A 把他的拒绝当成定局，却从未说明他在冒什么风险，这样的拒绝不构成知情拒绝。选项 B 是用恐吓施压，会破坏信任，往往让患者更坚决地拒绝。选项 D 绕过了一位 GCS 15、神志清醒、定向力正常、因而有能力自主决定的患者——有决定能力的成年人，家属不能代他签同意。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.27; CPCF area B
questions.evolutionEn: This exchange took place on scene, before the collar was applied and before he agreed to be transported.
questions.evolutionZh: 这段对话发生在现场，在上颈托之前、也在他同意转运之前。

passages.titleEn: Chest pressure in the kitchen after supper
passages.titleZh: 晚饭后在厨房出现胸部压迫感

profile.chiefComplaintEn: Central chest pressure for 40 minutes, radiating to the jaw, with nausea
profile.chiefComplaintZh: 胸骨后压迫感持续 40 分钟，向下颌放射，伴恶心
profile.pastMedicalHxEn: Type 2 diabetes; high cholesterol; hysterectomy 15 years ago
profile.pastMedicalHxZh: 2 型糖尿病；高胆固醇；15 年前子宫切除术
profile.medicationsEn: Metformin; atorvastatin. No nitroglycerin has ever been prescribed for her
profile.firstVitalsEn: HR 96 and regular; RR 22; BP 104/68; SpO2 95% on room air; BGL 8.2 mmol/L; Temp 36.8 C
profile.firstVitalsZh: HR 96，规则；RR 22；BP 104/68；室内空气下 SpO2 95%；BGL 8.2 mmol/L；体温 36.8 C
profile.physicalFindingsEn: Pale, cool, clammy skin; sitting forward on a kitchen chair; lungs clear on auscultation; no peripheral edema
profile.physicalFindingsZh: 皮肤苍白、湿冷；坐在厨房椅子上身体前倾；听诊双肺清；无下肢水肿
profile.otherInformationEn: She has taken nothing before your arrival and has no known allergies. She says she "feels ridiculous" for calling and has twice asked whether she could just drive herself to a walk-in clinic.
profile.otherInformationZh: 你们到达前她没有服用任何药物，无已知过敏史。她说自己叫救护车「实在太小题大做」，并已两次问能不能自己开车去走诊诊所。

questions.questionEn: Which one of the following is the correct EMR dose and route of Aspirin for this patient?
questions.questionZh: 对这位患者，EMR 给 Aspirin 的正确剂量与途径是以下哪一项？

options.en: 81 mg swallowed whole with water
options.zh: 81 mg，用水整片吞服

options.en: 160 mg chewed and swallowed
options.zh: 160 mg，嚼碎后吞下

options.en: 325 mg placed under the tongue
options.zh: 325 mg，舌下含服

options.en: 650 mg chewed and swallowed
options.zh: 650 mg，嚼碎后吞下

questions.explanationEn: The BC monograph gives 160 mg PO, chewed and swallowed. Chewing matters: it speeds absorption, which is the whole point in a suspected coronary event. Swallowing a tablet whole (option A) delays the effect and 81 mg is below the dose specified. Aspirin is not given sublingually, so option C is wrong on both count and route, and option D exceeds the specified dose. Aspirin is also the one medication for which vital signs are not required before administration, though her contraindications must still be checked.
questions.explanationZh: BC 药物专论规定为 160 mg 口服，嚼碎后吞下。「嚼」很关键：这样吸收更快，而在疑似冠脉事件中，快就是全部意义所在。整片吞服（选项 A）会延迟起效，而且 81 mg 低于规定剂量。Aspirin 不经舌下给药，所以选项 C 剂量和途径都不对；选项 D 超出规定剂量。Aspirin 也是唯一一种给药前不要求先测生命体征的药物，但禁忌证仍必须逐条核对。

questions.questionEn: Aspirin has been given and she is on oxygen at 4 L/min by nasal cannula, with SpO2 now 97%. Repeat vitals are HR 98 and BP 102/64. She rates the pain 8/10. What is the most appropriate action regarding nitroglycerin?
questions.questionZh: Aspirin 已给，鼻导管 4 L/min 给氧后 SpO2 升至 97%。复测 HR 98，BP 102/64。她自评疼痛 8/10。关于 nitroglycerin，最恰当的处置是什么？

options.en: Give 0.4 mg SL and recheck the blood pressure in 3 minutes
options.zh: 给 0.4 mg 舌下含服，3 分钟后复测血压

options.en: Give 0.4 mg SL only after laying her flat to raise her blood pressure first
options.zh: 先把她放平以升高血压，再给 0.4 mg 舌下含服

options.en: Withhold nitroglycerin because her systolic blood pressure is below 110 mmHg, and initiate transport
options.zh: 因为她的收缩压低于 110 mmHg，暂不给 nitroglycerin，开始转运

options.en: Withhold nitroglycerin and give a second dose of Aspirin instead
options.zh: 不给 nitroglycerin，改为再给一剂 Aspirin

questions.explanationEn: Nitroglycerin is contraindicated at a systolic blood pressure below 110 mmHg, and hers is 102. The severity of her pain does not override a contraindication, so option A is the trap for candidates who treat the symptom rather than read the monograph. Option B manufactures a workaround the protocol does not offer, and laying a patient with chest pain flat to make a contraindicated drug usable is not a legitimate step. Option D repeats a drug whose dose is already complete. Withholding the nitroglycerin does not mean withholding care — she still needs oxygen titration, position of comfort, and prompt transport.
questions.explanationZh: 收缩压低于 110 mmHg 时 nitroglycerin 是禁忌，而她是 102。疼痛剧烈并不能压过禁忌证，所以选项 A 是给那些「看症状不看专论」的考生准备的陷阱。选项 B 自创了一个 protocol 里没有的变通做法——把胸痛患者放平，好让一个禁忌药变得「能用」，这不是正当步骤。选项 D 重复给一个已经给足剂量的药。不给 nitroglycerin 不等于不处置——她仍然需要氧疗滴定、舒适体位和尽快转运。
questions.evolutionEn: Aspirin 160 mg has been given, oxygen is running at 4 L/min by nasal cannula and SpO2 is 97%. Repeat vitals: HR 98, BP 102/64. She now rates the pain 8/10.
questions.evolutionZh: 已给 Aspirin 160 mg，鼻导管 4 L/min 给氧后 SpO2 为 97%。复测：HR 98，BP 102/64。她现在自评疼痛 8/10。

questions.questionEn: Because nitroglycerin is contraindicated, which one of the following analgesic options is available to the EMR for her chest pain?
questions.questionZh: 既然 nitroglycerin 是禁忌，以下哪一项镇痛方案是 EMR 可以用于她胸痛的？

options.en: Entonox, self-administered by inhalation
options.zh: Entonox，由患者自行吸入给药

options.en: Acetaminophen 1,000 mg PO
options.zh: 口服 acetaminophen 1,000 mg

options.en: Dimenhydrinate 50 mg IM for the nausea
options.zh: 为缓解恶心，肌注 dimenhydrinate 50 mg

options.en: Ibuprofen 400 mg PO
options.zh: 口服 ibuprofen 400 mg

questions.explanationEn: One of the listed indications for Entonox is cardiac-related chest pain where nitroglycerin is of no value or is contraindicated, which is exactly this situation. She is alert, can follow instructions and can hold the mouthpiece herself, so she can self-administer. Option C is a PCP medication and outside the EMR scope. Options B and D are indicated for mild to moderate pain and pyrexia, not for suspected cardiac ischemia, and ibuprofen carries the additional problem of being an NSAID in a patient who has just been given Aspirin.
questions.explanationZh: Entonox 的适应证之一，正是「nitroglycerin 无效或属禁忌时的心源性胸痛」，本例恰好符合。她神志清醒、能听懂指令、能自己拿住吸嘴，因此可以自行吸入给药。选项 C 是 PCP 级别药物，超出 EMR 范围。选项 B、D 的适应证是轻中度疼痛和发热，而不是疑似心肌缺血；ibuprofen 还多一层问题——她刚服过 Aspirin，再叠加一种 NSAID 并不合适。
questions.evolutionEn: Nitroglycerin has been withheld because of the systolic blood pressure of 102 mmHg. Her pain remains 8/10.
questions.evolutionZh: 因收缩压 102 mmHg，已决定不给 nitroglycerin。她的疼痛仍为 8/10。

questions.questionEn: As you prepare to move her she says: "Honestly, I feel ridiculous. It's probably just heartburn from the curry. Let me drive myself to the walk-in clinic and you can go to a real emergency." What is the EMR's most appropriate response?
questions.questionZh: 在你准备搬动她时，她说：「说真的，我觉得自己太小题大做了。八成就是咖喱吃的烧心。让我自己开车去走诊诊所吧，你们去处理真正的急诊。」EMR 最恰当的回应是什么？

options.en: "It could be a myocardial infarction, an aortic dissection or pericarditis — none of those can be ruled out here."
options.zh: 「这可能是 myocardial infarction、aortic dissection 或 pericarditis——这些在现场都排除不了。」

options.en: "If you feel well enough to drive, that's your call — the walk-in clinic can always send you on."
options.zh: 「如果您觉得自己开得了车，那就随您——走诊诊所觉得不行还可以再转您去。」

options.en: "Let me help you find your keys and I'll follow behind you in the ambulance."
options.zh: 「我帮您找钥匙，我开救护车跟在您后面。」

options.en: "You're not taking us away from anyone — this is exactly what we're for. The pain you're describing may be coming from your heart, and if it is, driving yourself is dangerous. We need to take you in by ambulance."
options.zh: 「您没有占用谁的资源——我们就是为这种情况存在的。您描述的这种痛可能来自心脏，如果是的话，自己开车非常危险。我们需要用救护车送您过去。」

questions.explanationEn: Both halves have to be right. Option D answers the worry she actually voiced — that she is wasting the crew's time — and then states clearly that she must go by ambulance. Option A is clinically accurate but delivered in medical jargon that will frighten rather than inform her. Options B and C are kind in tone but both end with a patient in suspected cardiac ischemia driving a car, and a patient who arrests at the wheel endangers herself and everyone on the road. An answer that is warm but leaves a possible MI patient driving is always wrong.
questions.explanationZh: 两半都必须对。选项 D 回应了她真正说出口的顾虑——怕自己浪费了急救资源——然后明确告诉她必须乘救护车走。选项 A 临床上没错，但用的是医学术语，只会吓到她而不是让她理解。选项 B 和 C 语气都很温和，但结局都是让一个疑似心肌缺血的患者自己开车；一旦在方向盘后面发生心脏骤停，害的不只是她自己，还有路上所有人。语气再暖，只要让可能是 MI 的患者自己开车，就一定是错的。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.47; CPCF area B
questions.evolutionEn: Aspirin and Entonox have been given, nitroglycerin has been withheld, and the crew is preparing to move her to the stretcher.
questions.evolutionZh: 已给 Aspirin 和 Entonox，nitroglycerin 未给；急救组正准备把她搬上担架。

passages.titleEn: Two-vehicle collision on a highway off-ramp
passages.titleZh: 高速公路匝道上的两车相撞
passages.passageEn: You and your EMR partner are first on scene at a two-vehicle collision on a highway off-ramp at 21:40. A pickup truck has struck the driver's side of a small sedan; the sedan's driver's door is intruded roughly 40 cm and the windshield is starred. The sedan's driver, a 34-year-old man, is still belted in his seat, awake, and shouting that his left leg is trapped and "killing" him. Traffic is still moving past in the adjacent lane, broken glass is spread across the roadway, and the pickup driver is standing at the roadside on his phone. Fire and a PCP ambulance are both twelve minutes out.
passages.passageZh: 晚上 21:40，你和 EMR 搭档是一起高速公路匝道两车相撞事故的首到单位。一辆皮卡撞上了一辆小型轿车的驾驶侧；轿车的驾驶门向内凹陷约 40 cm，挡风玻璃呈放射状碎裂。轿车司机是一名 34 岁男性，仍系着安全带坐在座位上，意识清醒，大喊左腿被卡住、「疼死了」。旁边车道仍有车流通过，路面散落着碎玻璃，皮卡司机站在路肩打电话。消防和 PCP 救护车都还有 12 分钟才到。

questions.questionEn: Before approaching the sedan, what is the crew's first priority?
questions.questionZh: 在靠近那辆轿车之前，急救组的首要任务是什么？

options.en: Ask the pickup driver what happened so the mechanism can be documented
options.zh: 先问皮卡司机事情经过，以便记录受伤机制

options.en: Reach the trapped patient quickly, since he is clearly the most seriously injured
options.zh: 尽快接近被卡住的患者，因为他显然伤得最重

options.en: Make the scene safe: position the ambulance to block the lane, put on high-visibility PPE and control the passing traffic
options.zh: 先把现场变安全：把救护车停成阻挡车道的位置、穿好高可视度防护装备、管控过往车流

options.en: Get the traction splint out, since a trapped leg suggests a femur fracture
options.zh: 先把牵引夹板取出来，因为腿被卡提示可能有股骨骨折

questions.explanationEn: The Rescue Scene Evaluation comes before the primary survey on every call, and its first two elements are hazards and environment. Moving traffic beside a crew kneeling in a doorway is the hazard that most often injures paramedics at collisions, and broken glass adds a sharps risk to every knee and hand placed on that roadway. Options B and D are both patient care, which is correct work at the wrong moment — you cannot treat anyone if you are struck. Option A is history taking, part of the secondary survey.
questions.explanationZh: 每一次出勤，Rescue Scene Evaluation 都排在 primary survey 之前，而它的头两项就是 hazards（危险源）与 environment（环境）。在急救员跪在车门口作业时旁边仍有车流通过，是车祸现场最常导致急救员受伤的危险源；散落的碎玻璃则让每一次跪地和撑手都带上利器风险。选项 B 和 D 都属于患者处置——事情本身没错，但时机错了：你自己被撞了，就谁也救不了。选项 A 是病史采集，属于二次检查的内容。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.9; CPCF area E

questions.questionEn: The scene is now secured. On the primary survey the patient is alert with a clear airway, RR 26, a present but rapid radial pulse, and cool pale skin. His left thigh is grossly deformed and his pelvis is tender when gently assessed. Which one of the following most clearly makes him a rapid-transport patient under the BC Guidelines?
questions.questionZh: 现场已管控完毕。初步检查发现患者神志清醒、气道通畅，RR 26，桡动脉可触及但快，皮肤湿冷苍白。左大腿明显畸形，轻柔检查时骨盆有压痛。按照 BC 指南，以下哪一项最明确地把他归为需要快速转运的患者？

options.en: His respiratory rate of 26
options.zh: 他 26 次/分的呼吸频率

options.en: His report that the pain is severe
options.zh: 他自述疼痛剧烈

options.en: The collision happened at night on a highway
options.zh: 事故发生在夜间的高速公路上

options.en: Intrusion of more than 0.3 m into the passenger compartment on the occupant's side
options.zh: 乘员一侧的车厢侵入超过 0.3 m

questions.explanationEn: The guideline lists specific mechanism-of-injury criteria that make a patient unstable regardless of how well they currently look, and significant intrusion of more than 0.3 m on the occupant's side is one of them. The door is intruded about 40 cm, which meets it outright. His cool pale skin would also qualify as a primary-survey finding of suspected shock, but among the four options given, the intrusion is the criterion stated verbatim in the guideline. A respiratory rate of 26 on its own is not on the list, pain severity is not a stability criterion at all, and time of day and road type are not either.
questions.explanationZh: 指南列出了一系列具体的受伤机制标准，只要符合，无论患者当下看起来多好都算不稳定，而「乘员一侧车厢侵入超过 0.3 m」正是其中一条。车门凹陷约 40 cm，直接达标。他湿冷苍白的皮肤同样可以算作初步检查中「疑似休克」的阳性发现，但在给出的四个选项里，车厢侵入是指南原文逐字列出的标准。单独一个 26 次/分的呼吸频率不在名单上；疼痛程度根本不是稳定性判定标准；发生时间和道路类型也不是。
questions.evolutionEn: The scene has been made safe. Primary survey findings are now available: alert, airway clear, RR 26, radial pulse present but rapid, skin cool and pale, left thigh grossly deformed, pelvis tender.
questions.evolutionZh: 现场已安全。初步检查结果：神志清醒、气道通畅，RR 26，桡动脉可触及但快，皮肤湿冷苍白，左大腿明显畸形，骨盆压痛。

questions.questionEn: Fire has extricated the patient onto a long spinal board. Repeat vitals are HR 128, RR 28, BP 86/60, with cool clammy skin. His left thigh is still grossly deformed. Which one of the following is most appropriate now?
questions.questionZh: 消防已将患者解救并固定在长脊柱板上。复测 HR 128，RR 28，BP 86/60，皮肤湿冷。左大腿仍明显畸形。此时最恰当的处置是以下哪一项？

options.en: Bind the pelvis, keep him warm and supine, and transport immediately without applying a traction splint
options.zh: 绑扎骨盆、保暖并保持仰卧，不上牵引夹板，立即转运

options.en: Apply a traction splint to the femur before moving, since traction reduces bleeding
options.zh: 搬动前先给股骨上牵引夹板，因为牵引可以减少出血

options.en: Apply a tourniquet high on the left thigh to control the internal femoral bleeding
options.zh: 在左大腿高位上止血带，以控制股部的内出血

options.en: Wait on scene for the PCP crew so that tranexamic acid can be given before transport
options.zh: 在现场等 PCP 组，先给 tranexamic acid 再转运

questions.explanationEn: The traction splint is indicated for suspected mid-shaft femur fractures in stable patients, and this patient is not stable: HR 128 with a BP of 86/60 and cool clammy skin is shock. He meets the pelvic binding indications outright — major mechanism plus a heart rate over 100 and a systolic under 90 — and binding reduces pelvic volume, tamponades bleeding and stabilizes fragments. The hypovolemia guideline then adds supine positioning, warmth and oxygen. Option B is the trap of a correct skill applied to the wrong patient. Option C cannot work: a tourniquet compresses vessels against bone in a limb, it does nothing for pelvic or intra-thigh bleeding, and it is not indicated without external hemorrhage. Option D holds an unstable trauma patient on scene for a PCP-only drug, which is both outside your scope and the wrong priority.
questions.explanationZh: 牵引夹板的适应证是「稳定患者的疑似股骨干骨折」，而这位患者并不稳定：HR 128、BP 86/60、皮肤湿冷，这就是休克。他完全符合骨盆绑扎指征——重大受伤机制加上心率 >100、收缩压 <90——绑扎可以减小骨盆容积、形成填塞压迫、稳定骨折断端。随后按 hypovolemia 指南补上仰卧、保暖和氧疗。选项 B 是「技术本身没错、但用错了患者」的陷阱。选项 C 行不通：止血带是把肢体血管压向骨骼，对骨盆或大腿深部出血毫无作用，而且没有外出血时并无指征。选项 D 让一个不稳定的创伤患者滞留现场，只为等一个 PCP 才能给的药——既超出你的范围，优先级也是错的。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.23, p.24, p.54, p.78
questions.evolutionEn: The patient has been extricated onto a long spinal board. Vitals have deteriorated: HR 128 (was 'rapid'), RR 28, BP 86/60, skin cool and clammy. The femur remains grossly deformed.
questions.evolutionZh: 患者已被解救并固定在长脊柱板上。生命体征恶化：HR 128（原为「快」），RR 28，BP 86/60，皮肤湿冷。股骨仍明显畸形。

questions.questionEn: The PCP crew arrives and joins you in the back of the ambulance. Which one of the following interventions performed on this patient is outside the EMR scope of practice?
questions.questionZh: PCP 组赶到并上了救护车后厢协助。以下针对这位患者的处置中，哪一项超出 EMR 的授权范围？

options.en: Applying a commercial pelvic binder
options.zh: 使用商用骨盆绑带

options.en: Establishing intravenous access and giving a 20 mL/kg fluid bolus
options.zh: 建立静脉通路并给 20 mL/kg 液体推注

options.en: Realigning a grossly deformed limb that has no distal pulse
options.zh: 对明显畸形且远端无脉的肢体进行复位对线

options.en: Applying a tourniquet to a bleeding extremity wound
options.zh: 对四肢出血伤口使用止血带

questions.explanationEn: Vascular access and fluid boluses are listed under Additional Primary Care Paramedic Interventions throughout the guideline, including in the hypovolemia protocol; they are not available to an EMR. Pelvic binding, limb realignment where the limb is pulseless, and tourniquet application all appear under interventions for all licence levels. On the exam these scope questions are worth the same as any other, and an intervention that is clinically sensible but above your licence is still the wrong answer.
questions.explanationZh: 在整本指南里，建立血管通路和液体推注都列在 Additional Primary Care Paramedic Interventions 之下，hypovolemia protocol 也是如此；EMR 不具备这项授权。骨盆绑扎、远端无脉肢体的复位对线、以及止血带的使用，都出现在「适用于所有执照等级」的处置里。在考试中，这类范围题与其他题分值相同；一项临床上说得通、但超出你执照的处置，仍然是错误答案。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.19, p.21, p.24, p.54
questions.evolutionEn: The pelvis has been bound, the patient is supine, warm and on high-flow oxygen, and transport is under way when the PCP crew joins you.
questions.evolutionZh: 骨盆已绑扎，患者仰卧、保暖并接受高流量氧疗，转运已开始，此时 PCP 组上车加入。

passages.titleZh: 从湖里被救上岸的 9 岁男孩
passages.passageEn: On a hot August afternoon you are called to a lake beach for a nine-year-old boy pulled from the water. Bystanders say he was jumping from a floating dock with friends, went under, and was not seen for about two minutes before a lifeguard brought him to shore. He is lying on the sand, coughing forcefully, soaking wet and shivering. One lifeguard is kneeling beside him; a second tells you the boy "went in head first off the dock". His mother arrives from the parking lot as you begin your assessment.
passages.passageZh: 八月一个炎热的下午，你被派往一处湖滨沙滩，一名 9 岁男孩刚被从水中救起。旁观者说他和朋友们从浮动码头往下跳，入水后沉了下去，约两分钟无人看见，随后被救生员救上岸。他躺在沙滩上，用力咳嗽，浑身湿透并在发抖。一名救生员跪在他身旁；另一名救生员告诉你，男孩是「头朝下从码头跳下去的」。你开始评估时，他母亲从停车场赶了过来。

questions.questionEn: Given the mechanism the lifeguard describes, what is the most appropriate initial management?
questions.questionZh: 考虑到救生员描述的受伤机制，最恰当的初始处置是什么？

options.en: Apply spinal motion restriction because of the head-first entry, keep him at rest, position him sitting up, and remove and dry the wet clothing
options.zh: 因为是头朝下入水，给予脊柱运动限制，让他保持安静休息、取坐位，并脱去湿衣物擦干

options.en: Roll him semi-prone immediately to drain the water out of his lungs
options.zh: 立即把他翻成半俯卧位，把肺里的水控出来

options.en: Lay him flat and perform abdominal thrusts to clear the swallowed water
options.zh: 把他放平并做腹部冲击，把吞进去的水排出来

options.en: Have him walk up to the ambulance to warm up while you take a history
options.zh: 让他自己走到救护车上取暖，你同时采集病史

questions.explanationEn: The drowning guideline bundles exactly these steps: spinal motion restriction as indicated by the mechanism, keep the patient at rest, position sitting up, remove wet clothing and dry the patient, avoid rough handling, and maintain body temperature. A head-first entry from a dock into a lake is a mechanism that cannot be cleared on a beach. Options B and C are the persistent myth that water must be drained or forced out; both delay real care and risk vomiting and aspiration. Option D directly contradicts "keep the patient at rest" and makes him move his own possibly injured spine.
questions.explanationZh: 溺水指南把这几步打包在一起：按受伤机制给予脊柱运动限制、让患者保持安静休息、取坐位、脱去湿衣物并擦干、避免粗暴搬动、维持体温。从码头头朝下跳入湖中，这样的机制在沙滩上是无法排除脊柱损伤的。选项 B 和 C 是「必须把水控出来」的老迷思；两者都在拖延真正的处置，还会诱发呕吐和误吸。选项 D 直接违反「保持安静休息」，还让他自己活动可能已受伤的脊柱。

questions.questionEn: Ten minutes later he has stopped coughing, says he feels fine and wants to rejoin his friends. HR 104, RR 22, SpO2 96% on room air, lungs clear. His mother asks whether he really has to go to hospital. What is the best reason to transport him?
questions.questionZh: 10 分钟后他不再咳嗽，说自己没事，想回去找朋友。HR 104，RR 22，室内空气下 SpO2 96%，双肺听诊清。母亲问他是不是真的必须去医院。支持转运的最佳理由是什么？

options.en: All children must be transported after any water incident, without exception
options.zh: 凡是发生涉水事件的儿童都必须转运，没有例外

options.en: He is likely hypoglycemic after swimming
options.zh: 游泳之后他很可能出现低血糖

options.en: He needs a tetanus booster after swimming in lake water
options.zh: 在湖水里游过泳，他需要补打破伤风疫苗

options.en: Pulmonary complications from a submersion can develop over the hours that follow, even in a patient who looks well
options.zh: 溺水后的肺部并发症可能在随后的数小时内才出现，即使患者当下看起来很好

questions.explanationEn: Water in the alveoli disrupts surfactant and irritates the lung, and pulmonary edema can develop hours after the submersion in a child whose lungs sound clear on the beach. Drowning is listed in the BC guidelines as a cause of pulmonary edema for exactly this reason, so a normal set of vitals now is not reassurance about the next few hours. Option A is an absolute-worded rule, which is usually the wrong answer and also gives his mother no reason she can understand or act on. Options B and C invent problems that submersion does not cause.
questions.explanationZh: 进入肺泡的水会破坏表面活性物质并刺激肺组织，肺水肿可能在溺水后数小时才发展起来，而此刻在沙滩上听诊肺部可以是完全清的。BC 指南正是因此把溺水列为肺水肿的病因之一——所以现在这一套正常的生命体征，并不能保证接下来几个小时也没事。选项 A 是绝对化措辞的规则，这类选项通常是错的，而且也没给母亲一个她听得懂、用得上的理由。选项 B 和 C 编造了溺水并不会引起的问题。
questions.evolutionEn: Ten minutes have passed. The coughing has settled, he says he feels fine, and vitals are HR 104, RR 22, SpO2 96% on room air with clear lungs.
questions.evolutionZh: 已过 10 分钟。咳嗽停止，他说自己没事，生命体征为 HR 104、RR 22、室内空气下 SpO2 96%，双肺听诊清。

questions.questionEn: During transport he becomes quiet and drowsy, his respirations become shallow at 34 per minute, and his SpO2 falls to 88% despite high-flow oxygen by non-rebreather. He now responds only to voice. What is the most appropriate action?
questions.questionZh: 转运途中他变得安静、嗜睡，呼吸变浅、频率 34 次/分，尽管已用 non-rebreather 给高流量氧，SpO2 仍降至 88%。他现在只对呼唤有反应。最恰当的处置是什么？

options.en: Apply CPAP at 5 cmH2O and titrate upward
options.zh: 上 CPAP，从 5 cmH2O 开始逐步上调

options.en: Sit him fully upright and encourage him to cough
options.zh: 让他完全坐直，鼓励他咳嗽

options.en: Begin assisted ventilations with a bag-valve mask and 100% oxygen, and notify the receiving facility
options.zh: 用 BVM 加 100% 氧气开始辅助通气，并通知接收医院

options.en: Reduce the oxygen flow rate, because high-flow oxygen is suppressing his respiratory drive
options.zh: 调低氧流量，因为高流量氧正在抑制他的呼吸驱动

questions.explanationEn: Shallow rapid breathing with a falling level of consciousness and a falling SpO2 on high-flow oxygen is failing respiration, and the guideline directs you to assist inadequate or failing respirations — for an EMR that means bag-valve-mask ventilation with 100% oxygen. Option A fails on two counts: CPAP is contraindicated in patients twelve years and under and in anyone whose level of consciousness is falling, and it is a PCP intervention. Option B leaves a drowsy child to do the work himself when he is already losing that fight. Option D is a myth misapplied from chronic COPD, and it would be dangerous here.
questions.explanationZh: 浅快呼吸 + 意识水平下降 + 高流量氧下 SpO2 仍在掉，这就是呼吸衰竭；指南要求对不足或衰竭的呼吸进行辅助——对 EMR 来说就是用 BVM 加 100% 氧气通气。选项 A 错了两层：CPAP 对 12 岁及以下、以及意识水平正在下降的患者都是禁忌，而且它属于 PCP 的处置。选项 B 是让一个已经打不动这场仗的嗜睡孩子自己继续硬撑。选项 D 是从慢性 COPD 那里生搬硬套过来的错误说法，用在这里很危险。
questions.evolutionEn: En route, he has deteriorated: quiet and drowsy, responding only to voice, respirations shallow at 34/min, SpO2 down to 88% on high-flow oxygen.
questions.evolutionZh: 转运途中病情恶化：安静、嗜睡，仅对呼唤有反应，呼吸浅、34 次/分，高流量氧下 SpO2 降至 88%。

questions.questionEn: He is still wet, is shivering and his skin is cold to the touch. Which one of the following is correct for the EMR?
questions.questionZh: 他仍然浑身湿透、在发抖，皮肤摸上去冰凉。以下哪一项是 EMR 应做的？

options.en: Leave the wet clothing in place as an insulating layer until arrival at hospital
options.zh: 把湿衣物留在身上当作保温层，直到送达医院

options.en: Remove the wet clothing, dry him, cover him with blankets and raise the temperature in the ambulance
options.zh: 脱去湿衣物、擦干身体、盖上毯子，并调高救护车内的温度

options.en: Rub his arms and legs vigorously to restore circulation
options.zh: 用力搓揉他的四肢以恢复循环

options.en: Give him a warm sweet drink as soon as he is able to swallow
options.zh: 只要他能吞咽，就给他喝一杯温热的甜饮料

questions.explanationEn: Both the drowning and hypothermia guidelines say the same thing: remove wet and cold clothing, dry the patient, cover with blankets or dry clothing, and warm the ambulance. Wet clothing conducts heat away from the body many times faster than air, so option A actively continues the heat loss. Option C is vigorous handling, which the hypothermia guideline warns against, and rubbing does nothing useful for core temperature. Option D gives an oral fluid to a child whose level of consciousness has already dropped once on this call, which is an aspiration risk.
questions.explanationZh: 溺水指南和低体温指南说的是同一件事：脱掉湿冷衣物、擦干患者、盖上毯子或干衣服、把救护车内加温。湿衣物带走体热的速度比空气快很多倍，所以选项 A 是在主动让热量继续流失。选项 C 属于粗暴搬动，低体温指南明确要求避免，而且搓揉对核心体温毫无帮助。选项 D 给一个本次出勤中意识水平已经掉过一次的孩子口服液体，存在误吸风险。
questions.evolutionEn: Assisted ventilation has been started and he is being transported; he remains wet, shivering and cold to the touch.
questions.evolutionZh: 已开始辅助通气并在转运中；他仍然湿透、发抖，皮肤冰凉。

passages.titleEn: Found in a driveway on a February morning
passages.titleZh: 二月清晨被发现倒在车道上
passages.passageEn: At 06:20 in February you are called to a rural driveway where a 79-year-old woman has been found lying beside her car. A neighbour says she left for an early appointment and must have slipped on the ice; the last time anyone saw her was 22:00 the night before. The outside temperature is -9 C. She is wearing a housecoat and slippers, she is not shivering, and she mumbles when you speak to her. Her skin is cold and waxy to the touch and her limbs feel stiff.
passages.passageZh: 二月的清晨 06:20，你被派往一处乡村住宅车道，一名 79 岁女性被发现倒在自己车旁。邻居说她本来要去赶一个早上的预约，应该是在冰面上滑倒了；最后一次有人见到她是前一晚 22:00。室外温度 -9 C。她穿着睡袍和拖鞋，没有在发抖，你对她说话时她只是含糊地咕哝。她的皮肤摸上去冰冷发蜡，四肢僵硬。

questions.questionEn: You cannot immediately feel a carotid pulse. What should you do?
questions.questionZh: 你一时摸不到颈动脉搏动。应该怎么做？

options.en: Begin chest compressions immediately, since any patient without an immediately palpable pulse is in cardiac arrest
options.zh: 立即开始胸外按压，因为只要摸不到脉搏就说明是心脏骤停

options.en: Take up to 30-45 seconds to confirm the absence of a pulse before starting CPR
options.zh: 用最多 30-45 秒确认确实没有脉搏，再开始 CPR

options.en: Check a radial pulse instead, since it is easier to find in a cold patient
options.zh: 改摸桡动脉，因为在寒冷患者身上更容易摸到

options.en: Apply the AED first and let the machine decide whether she has a pulse
options.zh: 先贴 AED，让机器来判断她有没有脉搏

questions.explanationEn: The hypothermia guideline makes a specific exception to the usual ten-second rule: take up to 30-45 seconds to determine pulselessness in a severely hypothermic patient. A cold heart can beat very slowly and very weakly, and starting compressions on a perfusing hypothermic heart risks provoking ventricular fibrillation. Option C is backwards — peripheral vasoconstriction makes a radial pulse the hardest one to find in this patient. Option D misunderstands the AED, which analyses rhythm and cannot tell you whether there is a pulse.
questions.explanationZh: 低体温指南在通常的「10 秒」规则之外做了专门例外：对严重低体温患者，可用最多 30-45 秒来判断是否无脉。低温的心脏可以跳得极慢、极弱；在一颗仍在灌注的低温心脏上开始按压，有诱发心室颤动的风险。选项 C 恰好搞反了——外周血管收缩使桡动脉成为这位患者身上最难摸到的脉搏。选项 D 误解了 AED：它分析的是心律，无法告诉你有没有脉搏。

questions.questionEn: A carotid pulse is found at about 40 and she is breathing 8 times a minute. She has been moved into the warmed ambulance and her wet housecoat has been removed. A tympanic temperature reads 27 C. Based on that temperature, what is the correct rewarming approach?
questions.questionZh: 最终摸到颈动脉搏动约 40 次/分，呼吸 8 次/分。她已被移入已加温的救护车内，湿睡袍也已脱去。鼓膜温度显示 27 C。根据这个体温，正确的复温方式是什么？

options.en: Actively rewarm with hot packs wrapped in towels and encourage mild activity
options.zh: 用毛巾包裹的热敷包主动复温，并鼓励轻度活动

options.en: Immerse her hands and feet in warm water to speed rewarming
options.zh: 把她的手脚泡进温水里以加快复温

options.en: Do not actively rewarm; insulate her to prevent further heat loss, heat the ambulance to 30 C and avoid rough handling
options.zh: 不主动复温；给她保温以防止进一步散热，把救护车加热到 30 C，并避免粗暴搬动

options.en: Actively rewarm with hot packs and warm blankets, but avoid any activity
options.zh: 用热敷包和温热毯子主动复温，但避免任何活动

questions.explanationEn: The BC guideline splits management by core temperature: mild and moderate hypothermia are actively rewarmed, but severe hypothermia below 28 C is not. At 27 C she is severe, so the plan is insulation to prevent further loss, an ambulance heated to 30 C, and gentle handling. Options A and D both apply the moderate-hypothermia plan to a severe patient, and option A adds activity, which pushes cold peripheral blood back to the core. Option B rewarms the periphery first, the same error in a more aggressive form. The stiff limbs and absent shivering in the passage were the clues that she was already below the shivering threshold.
questions.explanationZh: BC 指南按核心体温分档处理：轻度和中度低体温要主动复温，而低于 28 C 的重度低体温不主动复温。她 27 C，属重度，因此方案是保温以防继续散热、把救护车加热到 30 C、并轻柔搬动。选项 A 和 D 都是把中度低体温的方案套在重度患者身上，选项 A 还加上了活动——那会把外周的冷血推回核心。选项 B 先复温外周，是同一个错误的更激进版本。情境里「四肢僵硬」和「不再发抖」就是提示：她的体温已经低到连寒战都停止了。
questions.evolutionEn: A carotid pulse of about 40 has been confirmed and she is breathing 8 times a minute. She is now in the warmed ambulance, the wet housecoat has been removed, and a tympanic temperature reads 27 C.
questions.evolutionZh: 已确认颈动脉搏动约 40 次/分，呼吸 8 次/分。她已被移入加温后的救护车内，湿睡袍已脱去，鼓膜温度为 27 C。

questions.questionEn: Her respirations remain 8 per minute and shallow, and her SpO2 reads 86%. What is the most appropriate intervention?
questions.questionZh: 她的呼吸仍为 8 次/分且浅表，SpO2 显示 86%。最恰当的处置是什么？

options.en: Apply a nasal cannula at 4 L/min and continue to monitor
options.zh: 用鼻导管以 4 L/min 给氧并继续监测

options.en: Apply a non-rebreather mask at 15 L/min and continue to monitor
options.zh: 用 non-rebreather 面罩以 15 L/min 给氧并继续监测

options.en: Insert an oropharyngeal airway and let her breathe room air until she warms
options.zh: 插入 OPA，让她呼吸室内空气直到体温回升

options.en: Assist ventilations with a bag-valve mask and 100% oxygen at an appropriate rate, handling her gently
options.zh: 用 BVM 加 100% 氧气以适当频率辅助通气，同时轻柔操作

questions.explanationEn: A rate of 8 with shallow tidal volumes in a patient with an altered level of consciousness is the guideline's definition of inadequate or failing respirations, and the listed intervention is to assist those ventilations. Oxygen alone, whether by cannula or non-rebreather, does not fix inadequate minute volume — the patient is not moving enough air to carry that oxygen in, so options A and B leave the underlying problem untouched. Option C leaves her hypoxic on room air. Note that the assistance must still respect the hypothermia rule of gentle handling, since a cold heart is irritable.
questions.explanationZh: 意识状态改变的患者呼吸 8 次/分且潮气量浅，正符合指南对「不足或衰竭的呼吸」的定义，而对应的处置就是辅助通气。单纯给氧——无论鼻导管还是 non-rebreather——都解决不了分钟通气量不足的问题：患者本身移动的气体量就不够，氧气进不去，所以选项 A、B 都没碰到根本问题。选项 C 让她在室内空气下继续缺氧。要注意，辅助通气同样要遵守低体温的轻柔操作原则，因为低温的心脏很容易激惹。
questions.evolutionEn: Insulation is in place and the ambulance is at 30 C. Her respirations remain 8 per minute and shallow and SpO2 now reads 86%.
questions.evolutionZh: 保温已完成，救护车内温度已达 30 C。她的呼吸仍为 8 次/分且浅表，SpO2 现为 86%。

questions.questionEn: Six minutes from hospital she loses her pulse. CPR is started, the AED advises a shock and you deliver it. Over the next four minutes the AED advises and you deliver two more shocks, with no return of circulation. What should the crew do now?
questions.questionZh: 距医院还有 6 分钟时，她失去脉搏。CPR 已开始，AED 提示可电击，你实施了一次电击。接下来的 4 分钟内，AED 又两次提示可电击、你也都实施了，但自主循环仍未恢复。此时急救组应该怎么做？

options.en: Continue CPR without pausing to analyze or shock again, and continue rapid transport
options.zh: 继续 CPR，不再为分析或电击而暂停，同时继续快速转运

options.en: Stop resuscitation, since three unsuccessful shocks in a hypothermic patient indicate death
options.zh: 停止复苏，因为低体温患者三次电击无效就说明已经死亡

options.en: Continue the standard cycle of two minutes of CPR followed by analysis and a shock as advised
options.zh: 继续标准循环：2 分钟 CPR 后分析，按提示电击

options.en: Pause CPR for 45 seconds every two minutes to recheck for a pulse
options.zh: 每 2 分钟暂停 CPR 45 秒，重新检查脉搏

questions.explanationEn: The hypothermia guideline is explicit: in cardiac arrest, apply the AED and defibrillate up to three times if indicated, then continue CPR and transport rapidly — after three defibrillations, do not pause CPR for analyzing or shocks. A cold myocardium usually will not convert until it is rewarmed, so further shocks buy nothing while the pauses cost perfusion. Option C is the normal adult algorithm applied to a patient the guideline specifically carves out. Option B stops too early; hypothermia is a recognized reversible cause and intra-arrest transport is appropriate. Option D builds in exactly the long interruptions the guideline is trying to eliminate.
questions.explanationZh: 低体温指南写得很明确：发生心脏骤停时贴上 AED，如有指征最多电击三次，然后继续 CPR 并快速转运——三次除颤之后，不要再为分析或电击而暂停 CPR。低温的心肌通常在复温之前不会转复，因此再多的电击换不来什么，而每一次暂停都在损失灌注。选项 C 是把常规成人流程套在一个指南专门做了例外的患者身上。选项 B 停得太早；低体温是公认的可逆病因，边复苏边转运是恰当的。选项 D 恰恰制造了指南想要消除的长时间中断。
questions.evolutionEn: Six minutes from hospital she has gone into cardiac arrest. CPR is in progress and three AED-advised shocks have been delivered over about four minutes with no return of circulation.
questions.evolutionZh: 距医院 6 分钟时她发生心脏骤停。CPR 正在进行，约 4 分钟内已按 AED 提示实施了三次电击，自主循环仍未恢复。

passages.titleEn: Unresponsive in a bar washroom at 02:15
passages.titleZh: 凌晨 02:15 酒吧洗手间内的无反应患者
passages.passageEn: You are called at 02:15 to the washroom of a downtown bar for an unresponsive 26-year-old man. Staff found him slumped against the wall of a locked cubicle and unlocked the door for you. A friend says he "took something" about half an hour ago but will not say what. There is a used needle on the floor beside him. He is grey, his lips are blue, and you count 4 shallow breaths in 30 seconds. His pupils are pinpoint and a carotid pulse is present at about 110. The cubicle is narrow and the floor is wet.
passages.passageZh: 凌晨 02:15，你被派往市中心一家酒吧的洗手间，一名 26 岁男性无反应。店员发现他瘫靠在一个反锁隔间的墙上，并为你们打开了门。一位朋友说他大约半小时前「吃了点东西」，但不肯说是什么。他身旁地上有一支用过的针头。他面色灰白、口唇发绀，30 秒内你数到 4 次浅呼吸。瞳孔呈针尖样，颈动脉搏动约 110 次/分。隔间狭窄，地面潮湿。

questions.questionEn: What is the EMR's first priority for this patient?
questions.questionZh: 对这位患者，EMR 的首要处置是什么？

options.en: Give naloxone 0.4 mg IM immediately, since reversing the opioid will restore his breathing
options.zh: 立即肌注 naloxone 0.4 mg，因为逆转阿片作用就能让他恢复呼吸

options.en: Open the airway, suction if needed, and begin bag-valve-mask ventilation with 100% oxygen
options.zh: 开放气道、必要时吸引，并用 BVM 加 100% 氧气开始通气

options.en: Obtain a blood glucose level before any other intervention
options.zh: 在任何其他处置之前先测血糖

options.en: Complete a rapid body survey and a full set of vital signs before intervening
options.zh: 先完成快速身体检查和一整套生命体征，再做处置

questions.explanationEn: The narcotic overdose guideline puts the primary survey first and in order: manage the airway with positioning, suctioning and adjuncts as needed, support ventilations, and administer oxygen to keep SpO2 at or above 94%. Naloxone comes after that, and this is the single most-tested idea in opioid overdose: the patient is dying of hypoxia, not of opioid, and ventilation is what reverses hypoxia in the next sixty seconds. Option A is not wrong as a treatment, only as a first move — the drug takes minutes to work while the brain is anoxic now. Options C and D are assessment steps that belong after the airway and breathing are secured; a blood glucose is required in this protocol, but not before ventilation.
questions.explanationZh: 麻醉剂过量指南把 primary survey 放在最前面且有顺序：用体位、吸引和气道辅助装置管理气道，支持通气，给氧维持 SpO2 ≥ 94%。naloxone 排在这之后——这也是阿片过量最常考的一个概念：患者是死于缺氧，而不是死于阿片本身，而能在接下来 60 秒内逆转缺氧的只有通气。选项 A 作为处置本身没错，错在把它当成第一步——药物起效要几分钟，而大脑此刻正在缺氧。选项 C、D 是评估步骤，应在气道和呼吸被稳住之后进行；这个 protocol 确实要求测血糖，但不是在通气之前。

questions.questionEn: Ventilations have been started and his colour is improving. Your partner needs to move him out of the narrow cubicle and notices that the used needle is now lying under the patient's thigh. What is the safest way to manage the needle?
questions.questionZh: 通气已开始，他的面色在好转。搭档准备把他从狭窄的隔间里搬出来时，发现那支用过的针头现在压在患者大腿下面。处理这支针头最安全的做法是什么？

options.en: Pick it up in a gloved hand and hold it while the patient is moved
options.zh: 戴手套把它捡起来，搬动患者时一直握在手里

options.en: Move the patient first and pick the needle up afterwards
options.zh: 先把患者搬出去，之后再回来捡针头

options.en: Sweep it aside with your boot and carry on
options.zh: 用鞋把它拨到一边，继续做事

options.en: Use a tool or the lid of the sharps container to lift it without touching it, place it in a puncture-resistant sharps container, then move the patient
options.zh: 用工具或利器盒盖把它夹起、不直接用手接触，放入防穿刺利器盒后，再搬动患者

questions.explanationEn: An exposed contaminated needle under the patient must be controlled before anyone lifts him, and it should be handled without being touched by hand and placed straight into a puncture-resistant container. Option B is the tempting one — patient first — but a lift is exactly the moment when hands go under a thigh and knees go onto the floor, so the sharp gets you or the patient. Option A keeps an uncapped needle in the hand of someone doing a two-person lift on a wet floor. Option C leaves it loose on the floor for the next person. Gloves do not stop a needle.
questions.explanationZh: 压在患者身下的这支暴露的污染针头，必须在任何人抬他之前先被控制住，而且应当不用手直接接触、直接放进防穿刺容器。选项 B 很有诱惑力——先顾患者——但抬人恰恰就是双手伸到大腿底下、膝盖压到地面的那一刻，针头正好扎到你或患者。选项 A 让一个正在湿滑地面上做双人搬运的人手里握着一支没有护套的针。选项 C 把它继续散落在地上，留给下一个进来的人。手套挡不住针头。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.9 (Rescue Scene Evaluation - hazards); CPCF area E
questions.evolutionEn: Bag-valve-mask ventilation is under way and his colour is improving. The used needle is now under the patient's thigh and he must be moved out of the cubicle.
questions.evolutionZh: BVM 通气正在进行，他的面色在好转。用过的针头现在压在患者大腿下方，而他必须被搬出隔间。

questions.questionEn: After two minutes of effective ventilation his SpO2 has risen to 96%, but he is still not breathing on his own and remains unresponsive. His blood glucose is 5.8 mmol/L. What is the correct initial EMR dose of naloxone?
questions.questionZh: 有效通气 2 分钟后，他的 SpO2 升至 96%，但仍没有自主呼吸，也仍无反应。血糖为 5.8 mmol/L。EMR 给 naloxone 的正确初始剂量是多少？

options.en: 0.4 mg IM
options.zh: 0.4 mg 肌注

options.en: 2.0 mg IM
options.zh: 2.0 mg 肌注

options.en: 0.8 mg IM
options.zh: 0.8 mg 肌注

options.en: 4 mg IV
options.zh: 4 mg 静脉注射

questions.explanationEn: The BC monograph starts at 0.4 mg and escalates only if the endpoint is not reached: 0.4 mg, then 0.4 mg after three minutes, then 0.8 mg, then 2.0 mg, with the target being an SpO2 of at least 94% and a respiratory rate above 10. Options B and C are later steps in that ladder, not starting doses, and jumping to them produces an abrupt, agitated withdrawal that is harder to manage. Option D confuses two things: 4 mg is the intranasal dose, and intravenous naloxone is a PCP intervention. Note that his blood glucose was checked and is normal, so it is not the cause of his unresponsiveness.
questions.explanationZh: BC 药物专论从 0.4 mg 起始，只有在未达终点时才逐级上调：0.4 mg，3 分钟后 0.4 mg，再 0.8 mg，再 2.0 mg；目标终点是 SpO2 ≥ 94% 且呼吸频率 >10。选项 B、C 是这个阶梯上后面的步骤，不是起始剂量；直接跳上去会造成突然而剧烈的戒断反应，反而更难处理。选项 D 混淆了两件事：4 mg 是鼻内给药的剂量，而静脉给 naloxone 属于 PCP 的处置。另外注意，他的血糖已经测过且正常，所以低血糖不是他无反应的原因。
questions.evolutionEn: Two minutes of bag-valve-mask ventilation have raised SpO2 to 96%, but he still has no spontaneous respirations and remains unresponsive. Blood glucose has been checked at 5.8 mmol/L.
questions.evolutionZh: 经过 2 分钟 BVM 通气，SpO2 升至 96%，但仍无自主呼吸、仍无反应。血糖已测，为 5.8 mmol/L。

questions.questionEn: Three minutes after the first dose he opens his eyes, pushes the mask away and says loudly: "What the hell did you do to me? You wasted my whole hit. I'm not going to any hospital — leave me alone." What is the EMR's most appropriate response?
questions.questionZh: 第一剂后 3 分钟，他睁开眼睛，把面罩推开，大声说：「你们对我做了什么？我那一份全废了。我不去什么医院——别管我。」EMR 最恰当的回应是什么？

options.en: "You nearly died. If you don't come with us you'll be dead by morning."
options.zh: 「你刚才差点就没命了。你要是不跟我们走，天亮之前就死了。」

options.en: "Fine. It's your body — we'll pack up."
options.zh: 「行吧。你的身体你做主——我们收拾东西走人。」

options.en: "I hear you, and I'm sorry — you weren't breathing, so we had to. The medicine we gave you wears off in under an hour and what you took may not, and if that happens you could stop breathing again with nobody here. We'd really like to take you in and stay with you."
options.zh: 「我听到了，也很抱歉——当时你已经没在呼吸了，我们不得不这么做。我们给你的这个药不到一个小时就会失效，而你用的那个东西可能还没失效；真到那时候，你可能会再次停止呼吸，而身边一个人都没有。我们很希望能送你去医院，并且一路陪着你。」

options.en: "You should think about what you're doing to your family."
options.zh: 「你该想想你这么做对你家人意味着什么。」

questions.explanationEn: Option C acknowledges his anger without arguing with it, explains honestly why you intervened, and then gives the one clinical fact that actually justifies transport: naloxone has a shorter duration of action than most opioids, so he can re-sedate and stop breathing after you leave. It ends with an offer rather than an order, which is what keeps a patient like this talking to you. Option A is a threat, and threatening a patient who has just been thrown into withdrawal usually ends the conversation. Option B accepts a refusal without ever explaining the re-sedation risk, so it is not an informed refusal. Option D moralizes about his family, which is a judgement, not care, and will destroy any chance of him accepting help.
questions.explanationZh: 选项 C 先承接他的怒气而不与之争辩，诚实说明为什么必须干预，然后给出唯一真正能支撑转运的临床事实：naloxone 的作用时间比大多数阿片类都短，所以你们走后他可能重新陷入镇静并停止呼吸。它以「我们希望」而不是「你必须」结尾，这正是让这类患者愿意继续跟你说话的关键。选项 A 是威胁，而对一个刚被推入戒断状态的患者施加威胁，通常谈话到此为止。选项 B 在从未说明「再次镇静」风险的情况下就接受了拒绝，这不是知情拒绝。选项 D 拿他的家人做道德评判——那是评判，不是照护，只会彻底断送他接受帮助的可能。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.56, p.72; CPCF area B
questions.evolutionEn: Three minutes after naloxone 0.4 mg IM, he has woken, pushed the mask away, and is angry and refusing transport.
questions.evolutionZh: 肌注 naloxone 0.4 mg 后 3 分钟，他醒了过来，推开面罩，情绪愤怒并拒绝转运。

passages.titleEn: Team van rollover with five patients
passages.titleZh: 球队面包车侧翻，共 5 名伤者
passages.passageEn: You and your EMR partner are the first unit to arrive at a single-vehicle collision at 16:30. A passenger van carrying a youth soccer team has left the road and rolled onto its side in a ditch. There are five patients. The van is on its side but stable, the ignition is off, and there is no fire or leaking fuel. The next ambulance is fifteen minutes away and fire is eight minutes away. The patients are: (1) a 46-year-old coach, walking around the ditch shouting for help, no obvious injuries; (2) a 15-year-old girl who was not breathing until you opened her airway, then began breathing at 8 per minute; (3) a 14-year-old boy, awake, with an obviously deformed forearm, radial pulse present, crying loudly; (4) a 13-year-old girl, unresponsive, with no breathing after her airway was opened and no carotid pulse; (5) a 15-year-old boy, awake but confused, with a rapid weak radial pulse and cool clammy skin.
passages.passageZh: 16:30，你和 EMR 搭档是一起单车事故的首到单位。一辆载着青少年足球队的面包车冲出路面，侧翻在路边沟里。共 5 名伤者。车辆虽侧翻但姿态稳定，点火已关闭，无起火、无燃油泄漏。下一辆救护车还有 15 分钟到，消防还有 8 分钟。伤者情况：(1) 46 岁教练，在沟边来回走动大声呼救，无明显外伤；(2) 15 岁女孩，你打开气道之前没有呼吸，打开后开始以 8 次/分呼吸；(3) 14 岁男孩，清醒，前臂明显畸形，桡动脉搏动可及，大声哭喊；(4) 13 岁女孩，无反应，开放气道后仍无呼吸，颈动脉无搏动；(5) 15 岁男孩，清醒但意识模糊，桡动脉快而弱，皮肤湿冷。

questions.questionEn: As the first crew on scene with five patients and no additional resources for at least eight minutes, what is your first action?
questions.questionZh: 作为首到现场的急救组，面对 5 名伤者、且至少 8 分钟内没有增援，你的第一个动作应该是什么？

options.en: Begin CPR on patient 4, since she has the most immediate threat to life
options.zh: 先给 4 号做 CPR，因为她的生命威胁最紧迫

options.en: Complete the scene evaluation and a rapid triage of all five patients, then immediately update dispatch with the number and condition of patients
options.zh: 完成现场评估并对 5 名伤者快速分诊，随即立刻向调度通报伤者数量与伤情

options.en: Start treating patient 2, since she is the most salvageable critical patient
options.zh: 先处置 2 号，因为她是最有救治希望的危重患者

options.en: Load patients 2 and 5 and begin transport before the other crews arrive
options.zh: 在其他单位到达前先装载 2 号和 5 号并开始转运

questions.explanationEn: The Rescue Scene Evaluation includes identifying the additional resources required, and with five patients and two EMRs the single action that changes the outcome for the most people is an accurate early call for help. Until dispatch knows there are five patients — three of them serious — the response they have sent is built on a one-patient collision. Triage also has to precede treatment, because the moment you kneel down beside one patient you stop being available to the other four. Options A and C are treatment decisions made before anyone knows what is on scene, and option D removes the only crew on scene from four remaining patients.
questions.explanationZh: Rescue Scene Evaluation 本身就包含判断所需的增援资源；面对 5 名伤者和 2 名 EMR，唯一能改变最多人结局的动作，就是尽早、准确地呼叫增援。在调度知道现场有 5 名伤者、其中 3 名危重之前，他们派出的力量是按「单人车祸」配置的。分诊也必须在处置之前，因为你一旦在某一名伤者身旁跪下，就等于对另外四人不再可用。选项 A、C 是在还没人知道现场全貌时就做出的处置决定；选项 D 则把现场唯一的急救组带走，丢下剩余四名伤者。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.9; CPCF area C

questions.questionEn: Dispatch has been updated and two more ambulances plus fire are en route. Which patient should receive your first hands-on treatment?
questions.questionZh: 已向调度通报，另外两辆救护车和消防正在赶来。你应该先对哪名伤者动手处置？

options.en: Patient 3, the 14-year-old with the deformed forearm, because he is in visible pain
options.zh: 3 号，前臂畸形的 14 岁男孩，因为他的疼痛最明显

options.en: Patient 4, the 13-year-old in cardiac arrest, because cardiac arrest is always the highest priority
options.zh: 4 号，心脏骤停的 13 岁女孩，因为心脏骤停永远是最高优先级

options.en: Patient 1, the coach, because once he is checked he can help you with the others
options.zh: 1 号教练，因为先把他检查完，他就能帮你照看其他人

options.en: Patient 2, the 15-year-old girl whose breathing returned as soon as her airway was opened
options.zh: 2 号，那名一开放气道就恢复呼吸的 15 岁女孩

questions.explanationEn: The purpose of the primary survey is to find and manage life threats, and when two providers face five patients the rule is the greatest good for the greatest number. Patient 2 has already proved that a simple airway manoeuvre keeps her alive, and at 8 breaths per minute she needs assisted ventilation now — she is the patient your hands can actually save. Patient 4 is a traumatic arrest who did not breathe even after her airway was opened; with two providers and four other patients, committing both of you to a CPR that has almost no chance and abandons three salvageable patients is the wrong call, which is why the wording "always the highest priority" in option B should stand out as an absolute. Patient 5 is in shock and is next, ahead of patient 3, whose forearm is painful but not life-threatening. Patient 1 is walking, talking and uninjured.
questions.explanationZh: 初步检查的目的是发现并处理危及生命的问题；当 2 名施救者面对 5 名伤者时，原则是「让最多的人获得最大的益处」。2 号已经证明了：一个简单的开放气道动作就能让她活着；而 8 次/分的呼吸意味着她现在就需要辅助通气——她正是你双手真的救得回来的那个人。4 号是创伤性心脏骤停，开放气道后仍无呼吸；在只有 2 名施救者、还有另外 4 名伤者的情况下，把两人都投入一场几乎没有希望、同时放弃三名可救伤者的 CPR，是错误的决定——这也是为什么选项 B 里「永远是最高优先级」这种绝对化措辞应当立刻引起你的警觉。5 号处于休克，是下一位，排在 3 号之前；3 号的前臂虽痛，但没有生命危险。1 号能走能喊，没有受伤。
questions.evolutionEn: Dispatch has been updated with five patients and their conditions; two additional ambulances and fire are en route.
questions.evolutionZh: 已向调度通报共 5 名伤者及各自伤情；另有两辆救护车和消防正在赶来。

questions.questionEn: Patient 2 is still breathing 8 shallow breaths per minute with her airway held open. She has a laceration on her forehead and does not respond to voice. What is the most appropriate management?
questions.questionZh: 在保持气道开放的情况下，2 号仍为 8 次/分的浅呼吸。她前额有一处裂伤，对呼唤无反应。最恰当的处置是什么？

options.en: Insert an oropharyngeal airway, assist ventilations with a bag-valve mask and 100% oxygen, and maintain manual in-line stabilization of the head and neck
options.zh: 插入 OPA，用 BVM 加 100% 氧气辅助通气，并保持头颈的徒手轴向固定

options.en: Apply a non-rebreather mask at 15 L/min and move on to the next patient
options.zh: 给她戴上 15 L/min 的 non-rebreather 面罩，然后去看下一名伤者

options.en: Sit her upright to improve her breathing and apply a hard collar
options.zh: 让她坐直以改善呼吸，并上硬颈托

options.en: Place her in the recovery position and reassess in two minutes
options.zh: 把她放成复原体位，2 分钟后复评

questions.explanationEn: She is unresponsive, which means she cannot protect her own airway, and she is breathing inadequately, which the guideline says must be assisted. An oropharyngeal airway is indicated for a decreased level of consciousness, and the forehead laceration is an obvious injury above the level of the clavicles in an unconscious trauma patient, so cervical stabilization is indicated in the primary survey and is maintained manually while you ventilate. Option B gives oxygen to a patient who is not moving enough air to use it and then leaves her alone. Option C sits up a patient with a suspected spinal injury and still does not address the inadequate ventilation. Option D is a reasonable position for a patient who is breathing adequately, which she is not.
questions.explanationZh: 她无反应，意味着无法自行保护气道；她的呼吸不足，而指南要求对不足的呼吸进行辅助。意识水平下降是 OPA 的适应证；而在一名昏迷的创伤患者身上，前额裂伤属于「锁骨平面以上的明显外伤」，因此初步检查阶段就有颈部固定的指征，并在通气过程中以徒手方式维持。选项 B 给一个连气都换不够的患者送氧，然后把她一个人留在那里。选项 C 让疑似脊柱损伤的患者坐起来，而且仍然没有解决通气不足。选项 D 对呼吸尚可的患者是合理体位，但她并非如此。
questions.evolutionEn: You are now with patient 2. Her airway is being held open manually, she is breathing 8 shallow breaths per minute, has a forehead laceration and does not respond to voice.
questions.evolutionZh: 你现在在 2 号身旁。她的气道正被徒手保持开放，呼吸浅、8 次/分，前额有裂伤，对呼唤无反应。

questions.questionEn: The coach (patient 1) follows you from patient to patient, repeatedly saying: "Tell me they're all okay. Please, just tell me they're all going to be okay — I was driving." What is the EMR's most appropriate response?
questions.questionZh: 教练（1 号）一直跟着你在伤者之间来回走，反复说：「告诉我他们都没事。求你了，就说他们都会没事的——车是我开的。」EMR 最恰当的回应是什么？

options.en: "They're all going to be fine, don't worry."
options.zh: 「他们都会没事的，别担心。」

options.en: "I can't talk to you right now, please step back."
options.zh: 「我现在没空跟你说话，请退后。」

options.en: "I can't promise you that yet — we're still assessing everyone. What would help me most right now is you: can you sit with the boy with the hurt arm and keep him still until the next crew arrives?"
options.zh: 「我现在还不能向你保证——我们还在逐个评估。但眼下最能帮到我的其实是你：你能不能去陪着那个手臂受伤的男孩，让他别乱动，一直到下一组人到？」

options.en: "You need to talk to the police about that when they get here."
options.zh: 「这件事你等警察来了跟他们说。」

questions.explanationEn: Option C does three things at once: it is honest without being cruel, it does not make a promise you cannot keep, and it converts an anxious walking-wounded bystander into a useful pair of hands, which is a real gain when two providers are covering five patients. Option A is a false reassurance about patients you have not finished assessing, and one of them has no pulse. Option B is dismissive of a man who is himself a patient and who will simply keep following you. Option D hears "I was driving" as a legal admission and answers as if the issue were blame, when what he needs is a task and a truthful answer.
questions.explanationZh: 选项 C 一次做成三件事：诚实而不残忍；不做你兑现不了的承诺；并把一个焦虑的、能走动的轻伤旁观者转化为一双有用的手——在 2 名施救者要覆盖 5 名伤者时，这是实打实的收益。选项 A 是对尚未评估完的伤者做出的虚假保证，而其中一人已经没有脉搏。选项 B 对一个本身也是伤者、而且只会继续跟着你的人来说太过冷淡。选项 D 把「车是我开的」听成了法律意义上的认错，回答的是责任归属问题；而他此刻需要的是一件事情做，和一个真实的回答。
questions.sourceRef: BC Guidelines p.9; CPCF area B
questions.evolutionEn: Patient 2 is being ventilated by your partner while you move to reassess patient 5; the coach has been following you throughout.
questions.evolutionZh: 搭档正在给 2 号通气，你转去复评 5 号；教练自始至终一直跟在你身后。
